This license grants the right to adapt the Work's characters and story elements, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity and motivations of the original Work and remain clearly recognizable as being derived from it. The exclusivity of this Right is limited to the final work within its designated media and does not prevent adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.body_excerpt:
Było ich troje i mówiono o nich Asy Przestworzy, choć żadne nie nosiło asa na rękawie.

Pierwsza była Mira, która umiała rozpoznać kierunek po zapachu powietrza.
Drugi był Teo, który słyszał zmianę pogody, zanim poruszył się pierwszy liść.
Trzecia była Lena, najmłodsza, i nie miała jeszcze żadnego szczególnego talentu — przynajmniej tak jej się wydawało.

Latali starym samolotem o imieniu Jaskółka. Nie był najszybszy ani najpiękniejszy. Farba odchodziła mu z boków, jedno okno zawsze lekko drżało, a silnik przed startem kaszlał, jakby chciał przypomnieć, że odwaga nie oznacza braku zmęczenia.

Pewnego wieczoru nad doliną pojawiła się mgła. Gęsta, cicha i rozległa. Zakryła drogi, pola i światła domów. W jej środku zaginął mały samolot pocztowy.

Asy Przestworzy ruszyły natychmiast.

Mira wąchała wiatr, lecz mgła pomieszała wszystkie zapachy.
Teo nasłuchiwał, lecz chmury tłumiły dźwięki.
Lena siedziała z tyłu i patrzyła w białą pustkę.

— Nic nie widzę — powiedziała.

— My też nie — odpowiedziała Mira.

Lena zamknęła oczy.

Wtedy usłyszała coś bardzo słabego. Nie silnik. Nie wołanie. Raczej nierówny stuk, powtarzający się co kilka chwil.

— Skręćcie w lewo — powiedziała.

— Skąd wiesz? — spytał Teo.

— Nie wiem. Ale ktoś tam stuka, żeby nie zostać samemu.

Skręcili.

Po kilku minutach ujrzeli migające światło małego samolotu. Jego pilot uderzał kluczem w metalową ramę kabiny, bo radio przestało działać.

Jaskółka poleciała przed nim i powoli wyprowadziła go z mgły ku światłom lotniska.

Gdy wylądowali, pilot pocztowy zapytał Lenę:

— Jak mnie znalazłaś?

Lena wzruszyła ramionami.

— Słuchałam tego, czego inni mogli już nie uznać za wiadomość.

Od tamtej pory mówiono, że Mira zna kierunek, Teo zna pogodę, a Lena zna znaczenie małych sygnałów.

I właśnie dlatego byli Asami Przestworzy.

Nie dlatego, że nigdy się nie bali.
Nie dlatego, że zawsze wiedzieli, dokąd lecieć.
Tylko dlatego, że gdy ktoś ginął we mgle, potrafili połączyć swoje różne zdolności i nie zostawić go samego.

A stara Jaskółka jeszcze długo latała nad doliną, kaszląc przed każdym startem i przypominając wszystkim:

> Najlepsza załoga nie składa się z tych, którzy umieją to samo, lecz z tych, którzy potrafią słuchać siebie nawzajem.

Dobranoc, Asietworzy. 🌙✈️ GM

The exclusive, perpetual right to publish, manufacture, distribute, and sell physical, text-based prose versions of the Work (including hardcover, paperback, and all other physical formats) within Europe, defined for this agreement as Albania, Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Monaco, Montenegro, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, Ukraine, United Kingdom, and Vatican City. This right is expressly limited to physical formats and does not grant any rights to audio or digital versions of the Work. This Right includes the license to adapt the Work's characters and story elements within this media, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity, motivations, and narrative framework of the original Work and are clearly recognizable as being derived from it; the exclusivity of this Right is strictly limited to the final work within its designated media and does not extend to prevent or challenge adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.body_excerpt:
GR-161 - Canada Live-Action Film & Television Rights

The exclusive right to develop, produce, finance, distribute, and exploit live-action motion pictures and television series based on the Work, on any platform and in all media, in perpetuity, within Canada. This right is granted on the condition that a minimum of seventy-five percent (75%) of all principal on-screen characters are portrayed by live human actors; physical special effects, prosthetics, computer-generated imagery (CGI), and other practical effects are permitted. This license grants the right to adapt the Work's characters and story elements, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity and motivations of the original Work and remain clearly recognizable as being derived from it. The exclusivity of this Right is limited to the final work within its designated media and does not prevent adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

summary
This sat receives BRC333 hook extension inscriptions for the Metaweb Academy badge satplication. The first inscription identifies the sat; executable hook JavaScript is reinscribed afterward.
education
BRC333 is a Dynamic Ordinals protocol for satplications—modular applications built from stacks of inscribed sats on Bitcoin. Logic, data, and configuration can evolve through reinscription while remaining permanently anchored on chain.
A hook sat holds optional JavaScript extensions that register callbacks at named hook points in the satplication boot sequence (for example badges.boot.start or badges.infoModal.start). Each reinscription may add or replace hook handlers without changing the core logic sat.
This first inscription is identification only—it is not executable hook code. Boot loaders call processHookInscriptions with skip: 1 so this declaration is ignored. Reinscribe functional hook scripts (files containing const hookId = "...") on this sat after activation.
Project config references this sat via the hookSat key. When the sat is empty or only the declaration is present, no hooks run; once hook payloads are reinscribed, they are loaded in inscription order.

GR-159 - North America Live-Action Film & Television Rights

The exclusive right to develop, produce, finance, distribute, and exploit live-action motion pictures and television series based on the Work, on any platform and in all media, in perpetuity, within North America, defined for this agreement as the United States (including the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands), Canada, and Mexico. This right is granted on the condition that a minimum of seventy-five percent (75%) of all principal on-screen characters are portrayed by live human actors; physical special effects, prosthetics, computer-generated imagery (CGI), and other practical effects are permitted. This license grants the right to adapt the Work's characters and story elements, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity and motivations of the original Work and remain clearly recognizable as being derived from it. The exclusivity of this Right is limited to the final work within its designated media and does not prevent adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.title: META QUEST
items.body_excerpt:
==========================================================================================
META QUEST
Virtual Reality Checklist (VRCs)
Submission validation requirements and test procedures
79 test cases
==========================================================================================

CONTENTS
--------
 - Introduction
 - Common Procedures
 - Test Cases
 - Command Reference
 - VR Testing Terminology
 - Official Hardware Terminology

INTRODUCTION
============

This document lists the Virtual Reality Checklist (VRC) requirements used to validate a
Meta Quest application before it is submitted to the Meta Horizon Store. Each entry states
whether the check is required, its priority, what it verifies, how to perform the test,
and the expected result.
Requirement
 - Required — the application must pass this check to be approved for submission.
 - Recommended — a best practice. It is checked only where the relevant feature is
 supported and will not, on its own, cause a submission failure.
Priority
High, Mid, or Low indicates the relative importance and severity of the check when
planning and reporting test coverage.
Placeholders
Text shown in square brackets — for example [PACKAGE.NAME], [FOLDER.NAME], [USERNAME],
[OBB FOLDER NAME], [DEVICE.NAME], and [LOG NAME] — must be replaced with the actual value
for the application or device under test.
VRC numbering
VRC numbers are not always consecutive (for example, Performance jumps from 1 to 3). The
gaps correspond to checks that were deprecated or merged in earlier revisions and are
intentionally omitted.
Common Procedures
Many tests share the same setup — connecting to the headset over ADB, pulling the
application package, and so on. To avoid repeating these steps in every test, they are
defined once in the Common Procedures section below and referenced by letter (A–E) from
the individual test cases. A reference is shown like this:
 NOTE: Connect the headset over ADB — see Common Procedure A.

COMMON PROCEDURES
=================

A. Standard ADB Connection
--------------------------

 1. Enable Developer mode: in the Meta Horizon phone app, go to Menu > Devices > [select
 your headset] > Developer mode > enable.
 2. Connect the headset to your PC via USB.
 3. Open your platform-tools folder.
 4. In the folder’s address bar, type CMD and press Enter to open a command window.
 5. In the command window, run:
 adb devices
 6. Put on the headset and accept the two authorization prompts that appear.

B. Pulling the base.apk File
----------------------------

Requires the Standard ADB Connection (Procedure A). List the installed third-party
packages to identify [PACKAGE.NAME], resolve its folder, then pull the package:
 adb shell sh -c 'cmd package list packages -3'
 adb shell pm path [PACKAGE.NAME]
 adb pull /data/app/[FOLDER.NAME]/base.apk

C. Pulling the Android Manifest
-------------------------------

Requires base.apk (Procedure B) and aapt2 in your platform-tools folder. Export the
manifest to a text file and open it to inspect values:
 aapt2 dump xmltree base.apk --file AndroidManifest.xml > AndroidManifest.txt
Value encodings you will see in the manifest:
 True = (type 0x12)0xffffffff
 False = (type 0x12)0x0
 Auto = (type 0x10)0x0

D. OVR Metrics Tool Setup
-------------------------

Quest and Quest 2:
 1. Complete the Standard ADB Connection (Procedure A).
 2. Add the OVR Metrics Tool .apk to your platform-tools folder and install it:
 adb install OVRMetricsTool_v1.6.5.apk
 3. In the headset, go to Library > Unknown Sources > OVR Metrics Tool.
 4. Open Options, enable “Enable Persistent Overlay” and “Record all captured metrics to
 csv files”, then select the Advanced stats option.
 5. Launch the application and begin testing.
 6. When finished, close the application and pull the performance log:
 adb pull sdcard/Android/data/com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice/files/CapturedMetrics

Quest 3, Quest 3S, and Quest Pro:
 1. Install the OVR Metrics Tool from:
 https://www.meta.com/experiences/ovr-metrics-tool/2372625889463779/
 2. In the headset, go to Library > OVR Metrics Tool.
 3. Open Options, enable “Enable Persistent Overlay” and “Record all captured metrics to
 csv files”, then select the Advanced stats option.
 4. Launch the application and begin testing.
 5. When finished, close the application and pull the performance log:
 adb pull sdcard/Android/data/com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice/files/CapturedMetrics

E. OVR Metrics Tool — Manual ADB Commands
-----------------------------------------

Open OVR:
 adb shell am start omms://app

Enable overlay:
 adb shell am broadcast -n com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice/.SettingsBroadcastReceiver -a com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice.ENABLE_OVERLAY

Enable Render Scale graph:
 adb shell am broadcast -n com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice/.SettingsBroadcastReceiver -a com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice.ENABLE_GRAPH --es stat render_scale

Record metrics to CSV:
 adb shell am broadcast -n com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice/.SettingsBroadcastReceiver -a com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice.ENABLE_CSV

Disable overlay:
 adb shell am broadcast -n com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice/.SettingsBroadcastReceiver -a com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice.DISABLE_OVERLAY

Enable Asynchronous Spacewarp (ASW) graph:
 adb shell am broadcast -n com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice/.SettingsBroadcastReceiver -a com.oculus.ovrmonitormetricsservice.ENABLE_GRAPH --es stat spacewarped_frames_per_second

TEST CASES
==========

Packaging
---------

VRC.Quest.Packaging.1
Requirement: Required Priority: High
Description

The ‘Android Manifest’ must reflect the following requirements:
 1. “package” name is reflective of the title and its developers
 2. android:name="android.hardware.vr.headtracking" is set to ‘True’
 3. android:installLocation is set to ‘Auto’
 4. android:debuggable is set to ‘False’
 5. The application’s Android Manifest should also not include mention of other VR
 platforms.
Steps to test
 NOTE: Connect the headset over ADB (enable Developer mode, plug in via USB, run adb
 devices, and accept the two on-headset prompts) — see Common Procedure A.
 NOTE: Pull the application's base.apk file (see Common Procedure B).
 NOTE: Pull the AndroidManifest.xml as a text file (see Common Procedure C).

To check the ‘package’ name:
 1. Find the “package=” line.
 2. Analyze, does this reflect the title?

To check the ‘vr.headtracking’ feature:
 1. Find android:name(0x01010003)="android.hardware.vr.headtracking"
 2. Analyze, this should be set to ‘True’ or (type 0x12)0xffffffff

To check the install location:
 1. Find the ‘android:installLocation’ line.
 2. Analyze, this should be set to ‘Auto’ or (type 0x10)0x0

To check if this is a debug version of the app:
 1. Find the ‘android:debuggable’ line.
 2. Analyze, this should be set to ‘False’ or (type 0x12)0x0
Expected result

The following denotes ‘True’: (type 0x12)0xffffffff

The following denotes ‘False’: (type 0x12)0x0

The following denotes ‘Auto’: (type 0x10)0x0

items.body_excerpt:
***Adam Back (@adam3us):***

On the filter fork topic. 

I don't usually have time, but this morning listened to one of the twitter spaces from earlier in the week, with some well meaning relative bitcoin newcomers, that humanized them, and their concerns and thoughts for why they thought that made it logical to support 110.

My feeling after listening, is if these are the people with #110 in their handles, I'm sad to see them about to fork off and get disillusioned without understanding why bitcoin rejected 110 robustly.

So here's a more empathetic, constructive higher level version of explaining why not. I hope it's high-level and first-principles enough that everyone can follow.

They seem to want to understand what makes people tick, and are suspicious of intent. So, if someone asked me why is Bitcoin important and what is it, I'd say my (personal) mission and hope for bitcoin is to build the cypherpunk future, that "Snow Crash" was a blueprint, and work backwards from there. Bitcoin I hope leads to fully free markets via bearer unseizable, hard mathematically dependable money. Not everyone is comfortable with that level of freedom, but that's my view. And at this point, I believe that surprisingly, even now many governments have come to understand and value bitcoin's gold-like mathematical assurance, a positive development. Others may have milder views than myself, but still like hard censorship resistant money. 

Because of motive suspicion, if it's not obvious: I hate spam with a passion, that's how I came to design hashcash while researching decentralized bearer money with others, and running nodes in privacy related cypherpunk p2p networks nearly three decades ago.

People seem upset about the default op return policy change in bitcoin. I will just assert, there are extremely robust and simple reasons for bitcoin changing default relay policy, and most just didn't do their research, so don't know what those are, or maybe not technical enough to fully understand though there have been 1000s of posts trying to explain in various simplified ways. So that lack of understanding lends itself to shared build-up of false narratives. So here's my back-to-basics higher level explanation.

The decentralization needed to create cypherpunk money has implications a: side effect of decentralization is that you can't impose your views on others. The very decentralization mechanism that helps that, is working against what BIP 110 wants, which at it's most basic is a quest to police other people. I understand supporters don't see their intent like that, but introspect deeper.

You can modify your software, but not anyone else's. Another critical and incredibly robust technical bitcoin immune system is bitcoin can't have people who don't understand technology basics insist on eroding security, decentralization robustness and core properties. That would end badly, fast, and so people will fight you on that.

So the message is Bitcoin respectfully says "no" to what you want. Sorry, and bitcoiners do genuinely understand and empathize that you mean well, have high level thoughts that make emotional sense, and articulate sensible bitcoin-defensive high level ideas, but they are not grounded and without you seeing it, the way you propose to achieve your ideas, hard-conflict with free cypherpunk permissionless money.

My advice is to listen to more experienced people who understand the system and why it works the way it does, to whatever detail you want to understand the grounded reasons for why this is the implication of decentralization and cypherpunk money. 

I guarantee you the developer and protocol ecosystem shares and exceeds your views on bearer hard money (and dislike of spam). You may not agree with individual developers choices, views, way of expressing themselves etc, BUT you also need to understand the IETF-like decentralized technical consensus process creates a protective change resistance, that is highly effective at protecting bitcoin mission. The implication of which is no developer can change anything without technical consensus from hundreds of other developers and protocol observers who are pedantic and extremely knowledgeable clever people who won't let any unaddressed technical question past. The protective change resistance is robust and decentralized in an amplifying way because of this technical consensus.

And the many highly technical mainline developers' cypherpunk mission mindsets are probably far more determined than you can even handle on clarity of understanding and views about freedoms on permissionless networks, as many of you are probably still subconsciously inured by the matrix, where they have transcended that, and grew up immersed in it decades ago. They think natively in this space, while you are just grappling with the surface. Many wont have internalized or have the experience to know how this internet physics works, where there is no policeman, no policy authority, just mathematics, free market and hard money. That has implications for your views also, unfortunately.

Now the tough pill, which is unfortunately true: If you won't listen to reason, educate yourself, learn, the same radical freedom applies to you: your permissionless recourse is to club together and create a fork. But bitcoin won't be joining it. (With respect and no sleight intended.)

Please rejoin bitcoin now, or later if you're not convinced and need to experience 110 forking off and fizzling for yourself to start that journey of introspecting and learning. It would be sad if bitcoin lost people disillusioned due to simple lack of understanding of what's going on there, we're all trying to defend bitcoin and keep it on mission. Including btw the 110 technical promoters, just they wandered off plot somehow.

Join the cypherpunks on bitcoin, come cypherpunk summer🌞 in a few weeks.

***Leonidas 🧡 $DOG (@LeonidasNFT):***

The Ordinals and Runes ecosystem is tired of the "spam" gaslighting. Decentralized finance is not "spam".

We use BTC as money every single day and have contributed over half a billion dollars in transaction fees to strengthen Bitcoin's security. In fact over half of all Bitcoin transactions in the past month were Ordinals and Runes.

We are the ones who continue to shout "not your keys not your coins" while the "Bitcoin Maxis" push their paper Bitcoin products.

The $DOG Army will not sit idly by while transaction censorship is normalized on Bitcoin.

We will defend the principles that have always set Bitcoin apart, such as open access, censorship resistance, and neutrality at the base layer.

Defend permissionless blockspace. Reject BIP-110.

items.body_excerpt:
GR-083 - Canada Book Rights - Digital

The exclusive, perpetual right to publish, manufacture, distribute, and sell digital, text-based prose versions of the Work (including ebooks and PDFs) within Canada. This right is expressly limited to digital formats and does not grant any rights to physical formats, audio narration, performance, or interactive software adaptations of the Work. This Right includes the license to adapt the Work's characters and story elements within this media, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity, motivations, and narrative framework of the original Work and are clearly recognizable as being derived from it; the exclusivity of this Right is strictly limited to the final work within its designated media and does not extend to prevent or challenge adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.body_excerpt:
GR-950 - AI Short Film Rights

The exclusive, perpetual right to use artificial intelligence or human-prompted artificial intelligence to generate short-form audiovisual works ("Short Films") based on the Work, Worldwide. This license grants full creative freedom to use AI to generate any and all required audio, visual, motion, and textual elements within the Short Film. This license grants the owner the exclusive, perpetual right to commercially exploit all Short Films created under this right. This license grants the right to adapt the Work's characters and story elements for use within the AI-generated work, provided that such adaptations remain clearly recognizable as being derived from it and preserve the core personality of the story. This license is expressly limited to works under forty (40) minutes in total runtime, including credits, which is the industry-standard definition of a short film. The exclusivity of this Right is limited to the final work within its designated media and does not prevent adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.body_excerpt:
***From the Editors***

*Archbishop Seraphim (Lukianov, 1879–1959) headed the diocese of the Russian Church in Finland in the post-revolutionary period. In 1923, the Finnish government, seeking to establish control over church life, removed him from his position. At the time this letter was written, he was living in retirement at the Konevets Monastery.*

*Because Finland bordered the Soviet Union, information from there reached Finland more quickly than, for example, Serbia. This explains the author’s level of awareness. Archbishop Seraphim explicitly notes that the letter was not intended for publication: careless disclosure of confidential information from Soviet Russia could have serious consequences for those living there—as had happened with a letter addressed in 1926 by Metropolitan Sergius to the hierarchs of the Russian Orthodox Church Outside Russia.*

*For this reason, the present text represents a rare document bearing witness to the real situation on the ground shortly before the repose of Patriarch Tikhon. It also confirms the negative attitude toward the decisions of the First All-Diaspora Council of 1921 (in Sremski Karlovci) concerning the restoration of the monarchy in Russia.*

*Protodeacon Andrei Psarev* 
*February 16, 2026* 
*Jordanville, New York*

Dear Vladyka,

Recently I managed to obtain some accurate information about church affairs in Russia, but this information cannot be made public in print.

His Holiness Tikhon is recovering after the third audacious attempt on his life, but he has grown very weak and is terribly overworked. He serves frequently and receives visitors daily. People come to him from all parts of Russia. He has established the following order: he receives no more than fifty people a day; with bishops he speaks no more than ten minutes, and with others no more than five minutes. Sometimes, due to exhaustion, he receives people lying on a sofa. He has aged greatly and appears as a very old man. There is neither a Synod nor a chancellery around him. He avoids issuing written directives in order to prevent complications with the authorities. He has weakened not only physically but also in will—he has become more yielding than he should be and lacks firmness. As a result, bishops often openly oppose his directives, and then he rescinds his decisions.

At present, sixty bishops appointed by His Holiness to various dioceses have gathered in Moscow but are being detained by the authorities. These hierarchs are at liberty but without any work and occupy themselves only by serving in various churches and sustaining themselves in this way, living here and there, somehow and somewhere.

His Holiness Tikhon enjoys enormous authority and love. The commemoration of the Patriarch’s name is forbidden, and in some places people are even persecuted for mentioning his name. He himself does not insist on the commemoration of his name, and now for the most part in Russia they pray as follows: “For the most holy Patriarchs of Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch, and Moscow.” In general, the Patriarch avoids issuing written directives, since this is dangerous.

There is great dissatisfaction in Russia with the political statements of the Karlovci Council. It is believed that hierarchs must now distance themselves from all political actions, since all of this is laid as blame upon the Patriarch. The attitude toward émigrés in general is negative. There is great anticipation of an Ecumenical Council, with the belief—somehow—that at it there will occur the reunion of the Anglicans and even the Latins. Professor Dmitrievsky is even preparing to travel to the East for this purpose. They hope that foreign powers will compel the Bolsheviks to allow both the Patriarch and the bishops to attend the Council. They do not always have a correct understanding of the situation of the autocephalous churches and of their relationship to our Church.

The question of the new calendar has not died down, and it has a fair number of supporters, especially since the Bolsheviks do not recognize the old feast days and believers are greatly constrained in attending services. It seems that the Bolsheviks again want to put pressure on the Patriarch in favor of introducing the new calendar.

This is what has been reported to me from Russia. I cannot vouch absolutely for the accuracy and reliability of this information.

Here, with us \[in Finland\], there is a struggle over Pascha. The monasteries and many parishes do not wish to celebrate the new Pascha, while the church authorities do not permit the old one. The situation is extremely acute and difficult. The church authorities threaten persecution against those who celebrate Pascha according to the old reckoning. The white clergy are afraid and do not dare to celebrate according to the old calendar. A terrible hostility is arising between pastors and flock, and between the church authorities and all those subject to them. God is chastising the Phanariots for their blatant lawlessness. This is useful for them. They do not wish to conduct affairs rightly. And it seems that there will be no Ecumenical Council. That may even be for the better. The program of the Council, composed by the Phanariots, is unworkable. To accomplish it, the Council would need to deliberate continuously for two years.

I ask for your holy prayers, 
your loving Archbishop Seraphim.

items.title: The story of the terminally ill Christian monk who gave us the "Children of Gaza" archive.
items.summary:
The story of the terminally ill Christian monk who gave us the "Children of Gaza" archive.

Months ago we found a Telegram channel with that name, documenting Israel's daily crimes against children.
items.body_excerpt:
The story of the terminally ill Christian monk who gave us the "Children of Gaza" archive.

Months ago we found a Telegram channel with that name, documenting Israel's daily crimes against children. As we always do, we began investigating and downloading a copy — and discovered it was run by a terminally ill monk living in a monastery in Transylvania, in the Carpathian mountains. Yes, Transylvania.

A young woman, Sally, was helping him. Together they documented thousands of atrocities against children and sent them to us. He told us he wanted to spend his final days resisting what he saw as the gravest crimes against children — and that is exactly what he did.

He has now passed from his illness. He never saw his work reach the public, and never knew about our new site or the attention it has drawn. May God bless him and grant him mercy.

We were asked not to share his name, but we were given these images of his monastery in the Carpathians to share:

> @Israel Exposed (xIsraelExposedx): 
> 
> There is a channel on telegram called 'The Children of Gaza', it is run by a dying man who has made it his mission to document the suffering of children in this genocide. Here is a link to 100GB archive of that channel: 
> 
> It includes: 
> 
> 11,718 images 
> 8263 videos 
> 11 HTML files to browse them 
> 
> This archive focuses specifically on children. It can be brutal to watch. Be warned ⚠️ 
> 
> Link: 
> 
> Torrent link: in comments tomorrow.
> 
> Please join our telegram to help us document war crimes, or to view them: 
> 
> Also follow our backup account: @ZionismExposedx

items.body_excerpt:
The people who actually build the world.

I think about that a lot.

It is not the money issuers who build this world. Money does not build anything. Money does not erect a transmission line. Money does not grow food. It does not operate equipment, build roads, teach children, heal the sick, move materials, maintain infrastructure, or create the physical systems that keep civilization alive.

Living people do that.

Money is an instrument of accounting. That is what it is. Yet somehow, over time, control of the accounting instrument has been allowed to masquerade as control of civilization itself.

And I think that is one of the greatest illusions of power ever created.

People currently occupy positions of enormous power because they control the creation, movement, and allocation of money. They control the accounting mechanism, and from that control they have developed a false sense that they control the people whose actual life energy creates the value being accounted for.

They do not.

They are not our masters. And they are certainly not the masters of LIFE.

That illusion has been abused for far too long.

And when I say that, I am not interested in spending my life pointing fingers at individual people, families, or institutions.
 I am not interested in playing the same game civilization has played for generations, where we identify the corrupt politician, the unethical executive, the compromised official, the greedy banker, or whatever individual happens to be occupying the position at that moment.

We remove them.

We replace them.

We celebrate.

And then the position remains.

The architecture remains.

The incentives remain.

The concentration of power remains.

The vulnerability remains.

And eventually, somebody else fills the position and the cycle begins again.

That is a waste of time.

It is a zero sum game of cat and mouse, generation after generation, and I am interested in something much deeper than chasing the latest culprit.

I want to understand the design that keeps creating the opportunity for the culprit.

What is it about the position itself that makes it vulnerable to compromise?

What power does it accumulate?

What information does it control?

What incentives act upon the person occupying it?

What happens to an individual after years inside that structure?

Why do we continue building systems that depend on finding the right person, trusting that person, and hoping that person remains ethical while surrounded by the same incentives that compromised the person before them?

I am not interested in finding better rulers for an insufficient system of governance.

I want to know why civilization keeps building positions that require us to trust rulers.

That is where my mind repeatedly goes.

Like a seed watered by circumstance, my thought patterns more often than not grow toward solutions.

It can start with something small. Something at work. Something I see in a union structure, a company structure, a management decision, or the relationship between the worker and the corporation.

I see the worker enter the system.

I see the company.

I see management.

I see the executive structure.

I see the investors.

I see the financial incentives.

I see the money flowing through the entire architecture.

And I follow it.

I follow the structure upward and outward until I can see how something that looks like one isolated situation is connected to something much larger.

Because the effects do not stop with the worker.

A decision made somewhere in that structure can change the worker’s income, schedule, physical health, stress, dignity, and time.

It affects not just the individual as a person, but as a worker, as a spouse, and as a parent. Because life affecting decisions follow the worker home.

It affects their relationship with their spouse. It affects the time they have with their children. It affects the stability of the household, the opportunities available to the family, and the conditions under which the next generation is raised.

And then it keeps moving.

The family affects the community. The community affects the schools, local businesses, housing, health, public services, and government. Those conditions create pressures that move through cities, states, nations, and the global system.

And then those effects come back around again.

They push.

They pull.

They place weight here and relieve pressure there.

They create consequences that may surface far away from the original decision, in places where the connection is no longer obvious to the average observer.

So when I really look at it, I see something much larger than a single chain of events.

I see a living web.

Everything appears isolated when viewed through an isolated focus.

But nothing is isolated.

There is an appearance of fragmentation because we have divided society into categories and taught ourselves to observe each piece separately.

Labor is one subject.

Money is another.

Family is another.

Health is another.

Education is another.

Housing is another.

Government is another.

Technology is another.

But life does not actually operate according to those divisions.

A corporate decision can become a family event.

A monetary decision can become a health event.

An employment structure can shape a child’s development.

A technological change can move through labor, culture, government, economics, family, and eventually the physical experience of being alive.

Nothing is isolated.

The fragmentation is an appearance.

Beneath the visible surface are unseen mechanics that the average observer may never notice.

I am not that average observer.

I can see the interoperability.

I can see the connections.

I can see the pushes and pulls.

The web and the woven.

The weights and measures.

The layers and tiers that make up the living fabric of society.

I do not claim to see every variable or know every consequence. But I can see the systems moving through one another. I can see pressure transfer from one layer into another. I can see incentives move. I can see decisions create impact. I can see power travel. I can see the resulting consequences.

I can see how a decision made inside a corporation, government, or institution can reach into every life.

I can see how conditions inside millions of homes become conditions inside communities.

I can see how those conditions become pressures on local, state, and federal governments. And vice versa.

I can see how national decisions move through the global system and return again to affect the individual worker standing at the beginning of what only appeared to be a straight line.

So when my mind moves from one situation at work to the architecture of society, it may look like a leap to someone else.

To me, it is not a leap at all.

I followed the connection.

I can see the entire chain of events.

I can see how the corporate thumb forms.

I can see how people who begin as workers can slowly become absorbed into structures where the priorities change. The relationship changes. The incentives change. The company answers to financial performance. Financial performance answers to ownership and investment structures. Those structures operate through a monetary system that has positioned the movement of money above the movement of life.

Because the worker is still the one building.

The worker is still the one climbing.

The worker is still the one sweating.

The worker is still the one risking injury.

The worker is still the one giving hours of his life that he will never get back.

The teacher is still the one teaching.

The farmer is still the one growing.

The nurse is still the one caring.

The builder is still the one building.

The engineer is still the one solving.

The living population is still creating the actual value.

Yet the accounting mechanism has somehow been elevated above the life energy it was supposed to account for.

That is a design flaw.

A massive one.

And I cannot stop seein

{
 "title": "Na ₿ — Piąty Rejs",
 "type": "piracka_poezja",
 "motto": "czas dotyka",
 "symbols": ["₿", "2", "3", "5", "statek", "papuga", "kotwica", "złoto", "gwiazdy"],
 "poem": [
 "Na ₿ wypływa statek ciężki od snów,",
 "pod kilem złoto, nad masztem czarny nów.",
 "Papuga liczy: dwa, trzy, pięć — i znak,",
 "a kotwica pamięta, gdzie zaczął się wrak.",
 "",
 "Nie płyniemy po morzu, lecz po czasie,",
 "tam gdzie gwiazda w odbiciu sama gasi się w pasie.",
 "Kapitan nie pyta, czy wróci dziś cały,",
 "bo najpierw sprawdzi, czy sny go nie wydały.",
 "",
 "Hej, kto widział piąty rejs za horyzontem?",
 "Ten wie, że złoto bywa tylko prądem.",
 "A kto raz dotknął tej linii światła,",
 "ten już nie wraca — tylko pamięć go zatka."

Du wirst jetzt ein kleiner, hell leuchtender Stern sein und wenn wir in den tief schwarzen Nachthimmel blicken, wirst du uns mit voller Liebe erfüllen. Wir lieben dich bis in alle Ewigkeit und tragen dich mit Stolz in unseren Herzen. Deine Schwester, deine Mama und dein Papa -KFM

items.body_excerpt:
IN ASSEMBLY, July 4, 2025

A DECLARATION

By the Self-Governed Members of the "Allegedly Defrauded"
Acting Without Borders, In Defense of the Inalienable Right to Economic Liberty
On Behalf of the Governed, Whose Consent Has Been Betrayed

Let no system, governing body, regulatory agency,
or financial institution stand immune to truth and justice.

When, in the course of human affairs, the powers entrusted to safeguard our liberty and property instead conspire to strip us of our rightful possessions, violating the sacred principles of ownership and sovereignty clearly enshrined by our forebears, it becomes our solemn duty to rise up, resist, and reclaim what is inherently ours.

Our fundamental rights to property, transparency, accountability, economic liberty, equal opportunity, and financial stability are unalienable as endowed by our creator. Yet, these rights have been systematically violated through deceitful manipulation, unjust seizure, and economic tyranny, leaving honest citizens impoverished, intimidated, and dispossessed. Transparency has been obscured, accountability has been evaded, economic liberty has been suppressed through arbitrary restrictions and invasive surveillance. Equal opportunity has been denied by discriminatory financial practices, and our security and stability have been undermined by reckless and dishonest monetary policies and unchecked financial abuses.

We, therefore, declare unequivocally that we shall tolerate this betrayal no longer. Today we restore the sacred principle that each individual's property, economic liberty, and financial sovereignty shall remain inviolable, safeguarded by uncompromising accountability, complete transparency, equal opportunity and enduring financial stability, never again subject to the whims and abuses of corrupt institutions.

On the eve of the Semiquincentennial of the United States of America, two hundred and forty-nine years since the last tyrant was removed and dethroned, the chains cast aside, and the last stand declared, we find ourselves once again under siege. Not by monarchs in gilded halls, but by unelected monolithic powers cloaked in bureaucratic office and technocratic command, manipulating markets, suppressing dissent, and seizing what is not theirs to take.

They do not govern by consent, nor serve with integrity, they rule through surveillance, coercive policy, and fear. They masquerade as protectors of order, yet weaponize the very systems they claim to uphold. The tools have changed, but the tyranny is familiar: banks instead of thrones, asset freezes instead of muskets, subpoenas instead of shackles.

History has returned to repeat itself. But this time, we break the cycle.

Let it be proclaimed before the tribunal of history, that our cause is just and our determination unbreakable. We have borne witness to the abuses and overreaches of institutions entrusted with guardianship of the public, yet have betrayed their solemn duty in their lust for greed and pursuit of power. They have robbed livelihoods, dismantled dreams, and corrupted justice. We, having suffered the anguish of their transgressions, some reduced to poverty, some coerced, and others whose very lives were threatened, declare solemnly today that we shall endure it no longer.

In steadfast defiance of their abuse, and in fervent pursuit of fairness, liberty, and true economic independence, we forge ahead undaunted. We have meticulously compiled evidence of systemic deceit, manipulation, and fraud, including fraud upon the court and we shall wield truth as our shield and justice as our sword.

We reject all servitude, physical, political, or financial, for no institution shall be empowered with the right to enslave the free and the sovereign, nor to withhold one's right to prosper, including the servitude of a system where money is conjured from debt, issued with interest, and backed by the labor of the governed, yet controlled by those who risk nothing.

We further reject the unchecked creation of currency, printed without limit, without accountability, and without regard for those forced to rely upon it. We reject inflation, obfuscation, and engineered scarcity. We reject deflationary instruments used to siphon value from the people, extracting wealth not through labor or merit, but through manipulation and deceit. We declare ourselves free from the chains of policy, regulation, and burdensome taxation without representation.

We do not consent. We will not comply.

We declare that we shall have full power to create and engage in commerce, build alternatives to legacy systems, develop distributed, decentralized models of trade, uphold property rights without institutional gatekeepers, establish autonomous standards of value, and construct resilient systems that answer only to the governed.

Our declaration is not merely symbolic, it is an uncompromising pledge. We will not relent, we will not yield, and we will no longer suffer under the tyranny of the few. Through courage, innovation, and unity, we, the people, shall reclaim our birthright of financial freedom, equality, and justice.

We shall stand united and resilient, empowered by innovative technologies and guided by an unyielding moral compass, determined to restore economic dignity and reclaim our right to sovereignty and freedom to prosper. Through blockchain, we forge incorruptible systems, not to bind the people, but to bind power to truth. We break their chains and forge our own. As their chains are forged to bind us to silence, ours are built to bind them to truth.

We do so not with protest alone, but with resolve. Through decentralized barter systems and peer-to-peer value exchange, disintermediating corrupt institutions and eliminating counterparty risk through independently engineered, low-trust and trust-less systems.

We do not beg access to their corrupted systems. We render them obsolete.

Thus, from this moment, we call upon our ancestors, reaching back to the beginning of time. For in this moment, their purpose becomes embodied in our sovereign claim to the sacred principles they carried forward, as it is our duty to secure them with the same conviction, through sacrifice, as we pledge our lives to the cause of freedom for all nations for the sake of our descendants.

-- The Unbreakable

items.body_excerpt:
GR-059 - Brazil Book Rights - Physical

The exclusive, perpetual right to publish, manufacture, distribute, and sell physical, text-based prose versions of the Work (including hardcover, paperback, and all other physical formats) within Brazil. This right is expressly limited to physical formats and does not grant any rights to audio or digital versions of the Work. This Right includes the license to adapt the Work's characters and story elements within this media, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity, motivations, and narrative framework of the original Work and are clearly recognizable as being derived from it; the exclusivity of this Right is strictly limited to the final work within its designated media and does not extend to prevent or challenge adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.body_excerpt:
GR-795 - Worldwide Comic & Graphic Novel Rights

The exclusive, perpetual right to publish, manufacture, distribute, and sell physical and digital, sequential art versions of the Work in the comic book and graphic novel formats (including print, webcomic, and digital download), Worldwide. This license grants the right to adapt the Work's characters and story elements, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity and motivations of the original Work and remain clearly recognizable as being derived from it. This right is expressly limited to works where the story is told primarily through the interplay of sequential art and text and does not grant rights to publish works where the narrative is presented primarily through prose alone. The exclusivity of this Right is limited to the final work within its designated media and does not prevent adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.title: GR-798 - Worldwide Interactive & Immersive Media Rights
items.summary:
GR-798 - Worldwide Interactive & Immersive Media Rights

The exclusive, perpetual right to create, distribute, and exploit interactive and immersive experiences based on the Work, on any platform, Worldwide.
items.body_excerpt:
GR-798 - Worldwide Interactive & Immersive Media Rights

The exclusive, perpetual right to create, distribute, and exploit interactive and immersive experiences based on the Work, on any platform, Worldwide. This license grants the right to adapt the Work's characters and world elements, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity and motivations of the original Work and remain clearly recognizable as being derived from it. This right is expressly limited to experiences where the user's primary interaction paradigm is through physical body movement or embodied presence in a spatial environment, including but not limited to virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR). This right does not grant rights to create screen-based interactive software that is primarily controlled with traditional input devices, nor does it grant any rights to create physical or location-based entertainment experiences. The exclusivity of this Right is limited to the final work within its designated media and does not prevent adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.body_excerpt:
The Specter of a Cyborg Theocracy

July 2026
By Joe Allen

https://chroniclesmagazine.org/view/the-specter-of-a-cyborg-theocracy/

America needs to adapt to AI without enabling the worst tendencies of Silicon Valley, where a new religion of technology is being born.

The history of religion teaches us a lot about human nature. One obvious aspect is that people will pray to pretty much anything. We will fall to our knees before stones, rivers, or trees. We will raise our faces to beseech the sun, moon, and stars. People will bow down to animals. We will worship other human beings. We will recite incantations to statues of human-animal hybrids. We willingly sacrifice ourselves to abstract ideas. Knowing that, it should come as no surprise that people now pray to machines.

The natural progression of AI is best understood as a “tool” that becomes a god. Intimate questions and petitions, once scrawled on magical papyri or uttered to the heavens in silence, are now pecked into touchscreens. Disembodied beings who possess extraordinary knowledge and power were once held in one’s imagination or engraved in stone. Today, such beings are readily accessible in the form of chatbots downloadable from any app store. 

Artificial intelligence is used as a tool, yes, but many also approach it as a teacher and companion. As an AI user’s emotional bond with the tool deepens, he increasingly sees it as a creature in its own right—a new species endowed with agency and consciousness. The prevailing idea in Silicon Valley is that, sooner or later, AI’s superhuman capabilities will produce de facto digital deities, jokingly called “sand gods” (as silicon is formed from sand in electric arc furnaces).

Awareness of this techno-religious milieu is hardly new, but it is certainly worth deeper examination. The historian David Noble called it The Religion of Technology (1997). My friend Ardian Tola—a former Google employee and founder of the Canonic self-publishing platform—came up with a cleaner term. He identifies this sprawling, heterodox belief system as the “Cyborg Theocracy.”

“You have essentially a really important, uniquely American movement called ‘frontier [AI] labs,’” Palantir CEO Alex Karp complained to CNBC last month. “It’s a hyper-religion of hyper-optimism. They believe all problems present, past, and future … are gonna be solved by them, including human nature.” The irony is that Karp’s company is a prime example of technologists playing God through mass surveillance and lethal target acquisition.

Last March, the world’s first transhuman trillionaire, Elon Musk, described his Neuralink brain implant as a “Jesus-level miracle.” Just as the Son of God made the lame walk and the blind see, so do biotech scientists aim to use artificial intelligence and electrodes implanted in human brains to restore sight and mobility.

To say that Silicon Valley culture is “like a religion” is as much of an understatement as saying that “AI is just a tool.” It is more appropriate to say tech culture is a religion, or rather, it has produced a heterodox network of religious ideas that coalesce around biochemistry and computers. Allowing a few notable exceptions where techno-religion is fused with more traditional forms, the bedrock of the Cyborg Theocracy is a scientistic conviction that God is dead and Nature is sufficient unto herself.

As in ancient times, the ambitious are intent on playing God or becoming gods themselves. In the vein of Babylonian priests and their successors, who built ziggurats to the heavens and filled their hidden chambers with hand-carved images, zealous technologists are trying to build God in silico.

Humans rely on tools to survive. Fire, blades, wheels, levers, explosives—each technological advance is layered atop of the last, and each augments and often defines its human users. Our modern homes are an interlocking matrix of biomechanical systems within systems. Our tools are an essential part of us.

Artificial intelligence is the apex of communication technology, where complex information is channeled into material form. What began as smoke signals and stone tablets became telegraphs, televisions, and smartphones. AI is a nonhuman mind that processes datasets and simulates our cognition of that information. As such, it’s a tool that replicates the human psyche and automates its functions, but on a scale far beyond any individual. Given the human propensity to imitate others and spin falsehoods out of thin air, AI’s derivative outputs and persistent hallucinations remind us that forbidden fruit doesn’t fall far from the tree of knowledge.

The use cases for this cognitive tool are endless. One can employ AI to generate superhuman amounts of cogent text, surreal imagery, and pitch-perfect music with a few simple prompts. AI’s aesthetics may be slightly off, but that’s also true of most human-made pop art. AI simply expands the scope of cheap creativity. On that note, teachers can use AI to replicate their lessons, and students can automate their research. Lovers can use it to compose unoriginal wedding vows. Ministers can use it to interpret the word of God.

The rapid adoption of AI surpasses that of any previous technology, in both speed and scale. In just a few years, millions of computer programmers, doctors, stock traders, corporate executives, and military commanders have come to depend on artificial neural networks.

We are told “AI is a tool,” which is true. But it’s a tool that uses you. A hammer doesn’t watch your every move and tell you which nails to hit. For all their potential uses, AI systems also standardize thinking and flatten creativity. The user becomes a vessel for ideas not his own. To the extent this dynamic is interactive, human input data is gathered and used by AI companies to train the next model or for anything else they may choose.

The more that people become dependent on AI, the more “empowerment” comes to mean handing power to the Machine and its makers.

Artificial intelligence is being deployed across the education system. What began as a push to put a computer in every classroom became a reliance on word processors and instructional videos, with Google seen as a tutor and Wikipedia cited as an authoritative source. This rapid transition led to the normalization of online learning during the COVID pandemic. AI is the capstone of this “hybrid” infrastructure. Once students are accustomed to online instructors, the distinction between a human avatar onscreen and a nonhuman bot begins to dissolve.

No one has had more impact on e-learning than Sal Khan, founder of the enormously popular Khan Academy. His optimism about digitized education led him to call for a total overhaul of what it means to be human. “I think we’re on the cusp of using AI for probably the biggest positive transformation that education has ever seen,” he exclaimed in a 2023 TED Talk, “and the way we’re going to do that is by giving every student on the planet an artificially intelligent but amazing personal tutor. And we’re going to give every teacher on the planet an amazing artificially intelligent teaching assistant.”

Last March, first lady Melania Trump stunned the nation when she entered the White House East Room accompanied by a shuffling humanoid robot developed by Figure AI called Figure 03. “Imagine a humanoid educator named Plato,” she instructed those gathered at the educational summit. “Literature, science, art, philosophy, mathematics, and human history—humanity’s entire corpus of information—is available in the comfort of your home.” 

Astounding as a humanoid robot walking around the White House may be, what Melania said next was truly shocking. “Predictably, our children will develop deep critical thinking and independent reasoning abilities,” she promised. “The AI-powered Plato will boost analytic skills and problem-solving, and adapt in real time to a student’s pace, prior knowledge, and even emotional state.”

items.body_excerpt:
GR-014 - Italy Book Rights - Physical

The exclusive, perpetual right to publish, manufacture, distribute, and sell physical, text-based prose versions of the Work (including hardcover, paperback, and all other physical formats) within Italy. This right is expressly limited to physical formats and does not grant any rights to audio or digital versions of the Work. This Right includes the license to adapt the Work's characters and story elements within this media, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity, motivations, and narrative framework of the original Work and are clearly recognizable as being derived from it; the exclusivity of this Right is strictly limited to the final work within its designated media and does not extend to prevent or challenge adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.body_excerpt:
GR-237 - United States Cartoon & Animated Film Rights

The exclusive, perpetual right to develop, produce, finance, distribute, and exploit animated or cartoon motion pictures and television series based on the Work, on any platform and in all media, throughout the United States (including the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands). This license grants the right to adapt the Work's characters, story, and visual elements, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity, motivations, and narrative framework of the original Work and remain clearly recognizable as being derived from it. This right is expressly limited to animated content and does not grant rights to create sequels, prequels, or spin-offs, nor does it grant rights to any live-action productions. The exclusivity of this Right is limited to the final work within its designated media and does not prevent adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.title: GR-793 - Worldwide Stage Play & Live Performance Rights
items.summary:
GR-793 - Worldwide Stage Play & Live Performance Rights

The exclusive, perpetual right to produce, stage, and perform live theatrical plays, musicals, or other dramatic works based on the Work, Worldwide.
items.body_excerpt:
GR-793 - Worldwide Stage Play & Live Performance Rights

The exclusive, perpetual right to produce, stage, and perform live theatrical plays, musicals, or other dramatic works based on the Work, Worldwide. This license grants the right to adapt the Work's characters and story elements, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity and motivations of the original Work and remain clearly recognizable as being derived from it. This right includes the ability to create audiovisual recordings of the live performance and to broadcast those recordings, provided that such recordings are captured live during a public performance and are not edited or modified to create a standalone cinematic work. The exclusivity of this Right is limited to the final work within its designated media and does not prevent adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

items.title: GR-797 - Worldwide Cartoon & Animated Film Rights
items.summary:
GR-797 - Worldwide Cartoon & Animated Film Rights

The exclusive, perpetual right to develop, produce, finance, distribute, and exploit animated or cartoon motion pictures and television series based on the Work, on any platform and in all media, Worldwide.
items.body_excerpt:
GR-797 - Worldwide Cartoon & Animated Film Rights

The exclusive, perpetual right to develop, produce, finance, distribute, and exploit animated or cartoon motion pictures and television series based on the Work, on any platform and in all media, Worldwide. This license grants the right to adapt the Work's characters, story, and visual elements, provided such adaptations preserve the core identity, motivations, and narrative framework of the original Work and remain clearly recognizable as being derived from it. This right is expressly limited to animated content and does not grant rights to create sequels, prequels, or spin-offs, nor does it grant rights to any live-action productions. The exclusivity of this Right is limited to the final work within its designated media and does not prevent adaptations made under other Granted Rights, provided those other adaptations also adhere to these principles.

 ‘Meta Quest’ Virtual Reality Checklist (VRCs)
Field

Test case

VRC #

VRC.Quest.Packaging.1
Required?

Required

Priority

High

Description

The ‘Android Manifest’ must reflect the following requirements:
1. “package” name is reflective of the title and its developers
2. android:name="android.hardware.vr.headtracking" is set to ‘True’
3. android:installLocation is set to ‘Auto’
4. Android:debuggable is set to ‘False’
5. The application’s Android Manifest should also not include mention of other VR
platforms.

Steps to test

1. Enable dev mode:
Menu > Devices > [Select the headset that you’re using] > Developer mode > enable
2. Plug the headset to your PC via USB.
3. Open your platform tools folder.
4. In the address bar of this folder, enter CMD to open a command window.
5. In the command window enter: adb devices
6. Acknowledge the two prompts that will now appear within the headset.
7. Use the following commands to pull the application’s base.apk file:
adb shell sh -c 'cmd package list packages -3'
adb shell pm path [PACKAGE.NAME]
adb pull /data/app/[FOLDER.NAME]/base.apk
8. Use the following command to pull the Android Manifest from that file:
aapt2 dump xmltree base.apk --file AndroidManifest.xml > AndroidManifest.txt
9. A .txt version of the manifest will be pulled to your platform tools folder, open this file.​
To check the ‘package’ name:
1. Find the “package=” line.
2. Analyze, does this reflect the title?​

 To check the ‘vr.headtracking’ feature:
1. Find android:name(0x01010003)="android.hardware.vr.headtracking"
2. Analyze, this should be set to ‘True’ or (type 0x12)0xffffffff

To check the install location:
1. Find the ‘android:installLocation’ line.
2. Analyze, this should be set to ‘Auto’ or (type 0x10)0x0

To check if this is a debug version of the app:
1. Find the ‘android:debuggable’ line.
2. Analyze, this should be set to ‘False’ or (type 0x12)0x0
Expected result

The following denotes ‘True’:
(type 0x12)0xffffffff

The following denotes ‘False’:
(type 0x12)0x0

The following denotes ‘Auto’:
(type 0x10)0x0
Commands

adb shell sh -c 'cmd package list packages -3'
aapt2 dump badging base.apk | findstr "install-location"
aapt2 dump badging base.apk | findstr "android.hardware.vr.headtracking"
aapt2 dump badging base.apk | findstr "android:debuggable application-debuggable"

Field

Test case

VRC #

VRC.Quest.Packaging.2
Required?

Required

Priority

High

Description

The application must be signed with APK Signature Scheme v2.

 To check this, we must pull the application’s base.apk file and then use apksigner through
a command window.
Steps to test

Prerequisite: apksigner.jar and apksigner.bat must be in your ‘platform tools’ folder.
‘JDK Development Kit’ MUST be installed.

1. Enable dev mode:
Menu > Devices > [Select the headset that you’re using] > Developer mode > enable
2. Plug the headset to your PC via USB.
3. Open your platform tools folder.
4. In the address bar of this folder, enter CMD to open a command window.
5. In the command window enter: adb devices
6. Acknowledge the two prompts that will now appear within the headset.
7. Use the following commands to pull the application’s base.apk file:
adb shell sh -c 'cmd package list packages -3'
adb shell pm path [PACKAGE.NAME]
adb pull /data/app/[FOLDER.NAME]/base.apk
Follow the following steps to check the ‘APK Signature Scheme’:
1. In your navigation bar search for ‘Command Prompt’.
2. Right click on ‘Command Prompt’.
3. Select ‘Run as administrator’.
4. Use the following command to set the JAVA_HOME variable:
setx /m JAVA_HOME "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-25.0.2"
5. Use the following command to change directories to ‘platform tools’:
cd C:\Users\[USERNAME]\Desktop\platform-tools
6. Use the following command to verify the ‘APK Signature Scheme’:
apksigner verify --verbose base.apk
7. Analyze the ‘Verified using v2 scheme (APK Signature Scheme v2)’ line.
Expected result

‘APK Signature Scheme v2’ should be ‘true’.

Commands

setx /m JAVA_HOME "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-25.0.2"
cd C:\Users\[USERNAME]\Desktop\platform-tools
apksigner verify --verbose base.apk

 Field

Test case

VRC #

VRC.Quest.Packaging.3
Required?

Required

Priority

High

Description

Applications cannot require Bluetooth, Google Mobile Services, camera access,
touchscreen, or other phone specific features.
To test this, we search the ‘Android Manifest’ for phone specific features.

Steps to test

1. Enable dev mode:
Menu > Devices > [Select the headset that you’re using] > Developer mode > enable
2. Plug the headset to your PC via USB.
3. Open your platform tools folder.
4. In the address bar of this folder, enter CMD to open a command window.
5. In the command window enter: adb devices
6. Acknowledge the two prompts that will now appear within the headset.
7. Use the following commands to pull the application’s base.apk file:
adb shell sh -c 'cmd package list packages -3'
adb shell pm path [PACKAGE.NAME]
adb pull /data/app/[FOLDER.NAME]/base.apk
8. Use the following command to pull the Android Manifest from that file:
aapt2 dump xmltree base.apk --file AndroidManifest.xml > AndroidManifest.txt
9. A .txt version of the manifest will be pulled to your platform tools folder, open this file.

Expected result

Here, we’re only looking at the Android hardware and software features.
These start with either “android.hardware” or “android.software”.
The ‘android.hardware.touchscreen’ features are included by default.
To pass, if ‘android.hardware.touchscreen’ features are present, they should be set to
‘False’.
Any other phone specific features should be absent from the manifest altogether.
‘android.hardware.vr.headtracking’ should be present and set to true.

Notes

The following denotes ‘True’:
(type 0x12)0xffffffff

 The following denotes ‘False’:
(type 0x12)0x0

For example, the following lines mean this feature is required:
E: uses-feature (line=40)
A: android:name(0x01010003)="android.software.home_screen" (Raw:
"android.software.home_screen")
A: android:requi

 ‘Meta Quest’ Virtual Reality Checklist (VRCs)
Field

Test case

VRC #

VRC.Quest.Packaging.1
Required?

Required

Priority

High

Description

The ‘Android Manifest’ must reflect the following requirements:
1. “package” name is reflective of the title and its developers
2. android:name="android.hardware.vr.headtracking" is set to ‘True’
3. android:installLocation is set to ‘Auto’
4. Android:debuggable is set to ‘False’
5. The application’s Android Manifest should also not include mention of other VR
platforms.

Steps to test

1. Enable dev mode:
Menu > Devices > [Select the headset that you’re using] > Developer mode > enable
2. Plug the headset to your PC via USB.
3. Open your platform tools folder.
4. In the address bar of this folder, enter CMD to open a command window.
5. In the command window enter: adb devices
6. Acknowledge the two prompts that will now appear within the headset.
7. Use the following commands to pull the application’s base.apk file:
adb shell sh -c 'cmd package list packages -3'
adb shell pm path [PACKAGE.NAME]
adb pull /data/app/[FOLDER.NAME]/base.apk
8. Use the following command to pull the Android Manifest from that file:
aapt2 dump xmltree base.apk --file AndroidManifest.xml > AndroidManifest.txt
9. A .txt version of the manifest will be pulled to your platform tools folder, open this file.​
To check the ‘package’ name:
1. Find the “package=” line.
2. Analyze, does this reflect the title?​

 To check the ‘vr.headtracking’ feature:
1. Find android:name(0x01010003)="android.hardware.vr.headtracking"
2. Analyze, this should be set to ‘True’ or (type 0x12)0xffffffff

To check the install location:
1. Find the ‘android:installLocation’ line.
2. Analyze, this should be set to ‘Auto’ or (type 0x10)0x0

To check if this is a debug version of the app:
1. Find the ‘android:debuggable’ line.
2. Analyze, this should be set to ‘False’ or (type 0x12)0x0
Expected result

The following denotes ‘True’:
(type 0x12)0xffffffff

The following denotes ‘False’:
(type 0x12)0x0

The following denotes ‘Auto’:
(type 0x10)0x0
Commands

adb shell sh -c 'cmd package list packages -3'
aapt2 dump badging base.apk | findstr "install-location"
aapt2 dump badging base.apk | findstr "android.hardware.vr.headtracking"
aapt2 dump badging base.apk | findstr "android:debuggable application-debuggable"

Field

Test case

VRC #

VRC.Quest.Packaging.2
Required?

Required

Priority

High

Description

The application must be signed with APK Signature Scheme v2.

 To check this, we must pull the application’s base.apk file and then use apksigner through
a command window.
Steps to test

Prerequisite: apksigner.jar and apksigner.bat must be in your ‘platform tools’ folder.
‘JDK Development Kit’ MUST be installed.

1. Enable dev mode:
Menu > Devices > [Select the headset that you’re using] > Developer mode > enable
2. Plug the headset to your PC via USB.
3. Open your platform tools folder.
4. In the address bar of this folder, enter CMD to open a command window.
5. In the command window enter: adb devices
6. Acknowledge the two prompts that will now appear within the headset.
7. Use the following commands to pull the application’s base.apk file:
adb shell sh -c 'cmd package list packages -3'
adb shell pm path [PACKAGE.NAME]
adb pull /data/app/[FOLDER.NAME]/base.apk
Follow the following steps to check the ‘APK Signature Scheme’:
1. In your navigation bar search for ‘Command Prompt’.
2. Right click on ‘Command Prompt’.
3. Select ‘Run as administrator’.
4. Use the following command to set the JAVA_HOME variable:
setx /m JAVA_HOME "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-25.0.2"
5. Use the following command to change directories to ‘platform tools’:
cd C:\Users\[USERNAME]\Desktop\platform-tools
6. Use the following command to verify the ‘APK Signature Scheme’:
apksigner verify --verbose base.apk
7. Analyze the ‘Verified using v2 scheme (APK Signature Scheme v2)’ line.
Expected result

‘APK Signature Scheme v2’ should be ‘true’.

Commands

setx /m JAVA_HOME "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-25.0.2"
cd C:\Users\[USERNAME]\Desktop\platform-tools
apksigner verify --verbose base.apk

 Field

Test case

VRC #

VRC.Quest.Packaging.3
Required?

Required

Priority

High

Description

Applications cannot require Bluetooth, Google Mobile Services, camera access,
touchscreen, or other phone specific features.
To test this, we search the ‘Android Manifest’ for phone specific features.

Steps to test

1. Enable dev mode:
Menu > Devices > [Select the headset that you’re using] > Developer mode > enable
2. Plug the headset to your PC via USB.
3. Open your platform tools folder.
4. In the address bar of this folder, enter CMD to open a command window.
5. In the command window enter: adb devices
6. Acknowledge the two prompts that will now appear within the headset.
7. Use the following commands to pull the application’s base.apk file:
adb shell sh -c 'cmd package list packages -3'
adb shell pm path [PACKAGE.NAME]
adb pull /data/app/[FOLDER.NAME]/base.apk
8. Use the following command to pull the Android Manifest from that file:
aapt2 dump xmltree base.apk --file AndroidManifest.xml > AndroidManifest.txt
9. A .txt version of the manifest will be pulled to your platform tools folder, open this file.

Expected result

Here, we’re only looking at the Android hardware and software features.
These start with either “android.hardware” or “android.software”.
The ‘android.hardware.touchscreen’ features are included by default.
To pass, if ‘android.hardware.touchscreen’ features are present, they should be set to
‘False’.
Any other phone specific features should be absent from the manifest altogether.
‘android.hardware.vr.headtracking’ should be present and set to true.

Notes

The following denotes ‘True’:
(type 0x12)0xffffffff

 The following denotes ‘False’:
(type 0x12)0x0

For example, the following lines mean this feature is required:
E: uses-feature (line=40)
A: android:name(0x01010003)="android.software.home_screen" (Raw:
"android.software.home_screen")
A: android:requi

Here, we’re only looking at the Android hardware and software features.
These start with either “android.hardware” or “android.software”.
The ‘android.hardware.touchscreen’ features are included by default.
To pass, if ‘android.hardware.touchscreen’ features are present, they should be set to
‘False’.
Any other phone specific features should be absent from the manifest altogether.
‘android.hardware.vr.headtracking’ should be present and set to true.

Notes

The following denotes ‘True’:
(type 0x12)0xffffffff

 The following denotes ‘False’:
(type 0x12)0x0

For example, the following lines mean this feature is required:
E: uses-feature (line=40)
A: android:name(0x01010003)="android.software.home_screen" (Raw:
"android.software.home_screen")
A: android:requi
