items.title: The Descent Into Nonbeing: From Covenant to Collapse
items.summary:
The Descent Into Nonbeing: From Covenant to Collapse

⸻

I. In the Beginning: God as Logos

Creation begins with structure.
God does not mold—He speaks. The Word divides light from darkness, sea from sky, land from water.
items.body_excerpt:
The Descent Into Nonbeing: From Covenant to Collapse

⸻

I. In the Beginning: God as Logos

Creation begins with structure.
God does not mold—He speaks. The Word divides light from darkness, sea from sky, land from water. Every boundary is born of breath.

“And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.” (Genesis 1:3)

Man is made in God’s image—not in matter, but in mandate:
to name, to remember, to steward, to mirror.

Covenant is not imposed—it is embedded.
To obey is to align. To rebel is to fracture.

⸻

II. The First Inversion: Rebellion as Knowledge

The serpent does not promise chaos—he offers divinity.

“And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:
For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened,
and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” (Genesis 3:4–5)

Obedience is recast as ignorance.
Desire becomes revelation.
Form is abandoned for self-determination.

The first lie is not “there is no God.”
It is “you can become one.”

⸻

III. The First Sacrificial Inversion: Cain and Abel

Abel offers blood—living sacrifice, submission to form.
Cain offers the work of his hands—clean, sufficient, self-shaped.

“But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.
And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” (Genesis 4:5)

Cain resents the favor given to pattern.
He kills his brother—not for gain, but to silence judgment.

This is the first murder.
It is also the first religious war.

Cain is exiled, but preserved.
He builds the first city—a civilization without altar.

Structure begins in rebellion.

⸻

IV. The Ark and the Rainbow: Covenant Through Judgment

The world fills with corruption.
Violence becomes the default language.

But one man obeys.

“Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.” (Genesis 6:22)

Noah builds a form before the flood arrives.
The ark is not symbolic—it is structure that saves.

The flood does not erase creation.
It resets the alignment.

“I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant
between me and the earth.” (Genesis 9:13)

It is not pride—it is restraint.
A promise sealed in light: mercy after judgment.

Now worn without memory.
The symbol reclaimed by those who deny the Flood.

⸻

V. Covenant and Circumcision: The Flesh Must Yield

God calls Abraham out of empire.
No idols. No tower. Only promise.

The covenant cuts deeper than command.

“This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee;
Every man child among you shall be circumcised.” (Genesis 17:10)

God marks the source of life.
Not to weaken—but to distinguish.

You are not beast. You are not your desire.
Even the power to create must pass through memory.

Circumcision sets the boundary:
You were made for covenant, not instinct.

⸻

VI. Law and the Pattern of Holiness

Through Moses, God gives the blueprint:
Tabernacle. Priesthood. Sacrifice. Sabbath. Time. Judgment. Mercy.

Each command is a shield against collapse.

Holiness is not moralism—it is ordered distinction.
Clean from unclean. Holy from profane.
Obedience from presumption.

But Israel rejects the pattern:
• They craft the calf.
• Demand a king.
• Embrace foreign gods.
• Desecrate the feasts.
• Pervert the altar.

The prophets warn. The people scoff.
And God gives them what they sought.

⸻

VII. Solomon and the Womb of Inversion

God gives wisdom to a king.
Solomon builds the temple. Fire descends. Glory fills it.

Israel has never been closer to heaven.

But the wise king turns.

“But king Solomon loved many strange women…
and his wives turned away his heart after other gods.” (1 Kings 11:1,4)

He builds high places for Chemosh and Molech.
He imports gods with dowries.
He mirrors Pharaoh more than Moses.

The altar remains—but the fire dims.
Worship fragments. Sacrifice continues without loyalty.

And something enters through the cracks:
• Names. Symbols. Seals.
• Incantations and diagrams.
• The roots of what will become magick.

Solomon’s legacy is divided—like the kingdom itself.
What was one becomes two. What was pure becomes possible.
The priesthood is polluted. The covenant is pierced.

Israel never saw a foreign idol it didn’t want to worship.
And now they’ve built temples for them in God’s own land.

This is the womb of inversion.

Babylon is not an invasion.
It is a birth.

⸻

VIII. Babylon and the Corruption of Covenant

God sends Israel into Babylon—not to destroy them, but to expose the fracture.

“Behold, I will send and take all the families of the north… and Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant…” (Jeremiah 25:9)

The temple is razed. Sacrifice ends. The presence departs.
What remains is memory—and memory begins to reshape.

Exile becomes absorption:
• Chaldean cosmology seeps into priesthood.
• Dualism and mysticism cloud the altar.
• Interpretation replaces obedience.

Scripture is still read—but layered in commentary.
Law is still cited—but filtered through councils.

By the time the temple is rebuilt, the scaffolding is already bent.

“Ye have made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.” (Matthew 15:6)

Interpretation replaces obedience.
Memory replaces presence.
The voice does not return.

The temple was rebuilt—but the glory never returned.
There was gold and ritual, but no fire.
No cloud. No Ark. No voice.

The priests stood in place, but the presence had departed.
The fire no longer fell. The voice no longer spoke.
The sacrifices continued—but the Ark was gone.
The rituals remained—but the glory had not returned.

By the time Christ entered the temple,
the priesthood still functioned—
but its center was hollow.

Rabbinic Judaism would rise only later,
built atop this vacancy—
a structure of rulings without fire,
preserved memory without presence.

And from that scaffold, others would grow:
Some hidden. Some global.
Some still bearing God’s name.

⸻

IX. Christ: Logos Made Flesh

The covenant is not discarded.
It is fulfilled.

The altar was defiled. The priesthood corrupted. The temple rebuilt—but hollow.
God does not repair the scaffold.
He descends into it.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” (John 1:1)

“And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us…” (John 1:14)

He does not send a new law.
He becomes the Law, alive.
He does not speak for the presence.
He is the presence, returned.

Christ walks the full pattern of covenant:
• Born under the Law.
• Circumcised on the eighth day.
• Baptized into priesthood.
• Tempted without falling.
• Teaching with authority—not citation.
• Consuming the scroll.
• Healing what the Law could only separate.
• Entering the temple—not to offer sacrifice, but to end it.

He is the priest, the lamb, the altar, the blood.

“Think not that I am come to destroy the law… I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.” (Matthew 5:17)

In Him, the covenant is transfigured:
• Circumcision becomes baptism—not of flesh, but heart.
• Sacrifice becomes communion—not repetition, but remembrance.
• Priesthood becomes intercession—not lineage, but appointment.
• The veil is torn. Access is opened.
• The temple is His body.
• The people are no longer ethnic, but aligned.

He fulfills every shadow:
• The ram in the thicket.
• The manna from heaven.
• The blood on the doorpost.
• The scapegoat.
• The tabernacle.
• The mercy seat.

Each was a placeholder. Now the pattern stands revealed.

He does not rebel against the structure.
He reveals its end.

The covenant passes through death—and does not dissolve.
It returns sharper.

He is the final sacrifice.
There will be no others.

He is the final priest.
No other mediation will be accepted.

He is the temple rebuilt in three days.
No third structure of stone will replace Him.

He is the seed of Abraham—not in descent, but in destiny.
All who are grafted into Him receive the covenant, fulfilled.

This is not a new religion.
It is the Logos returning to His own—unrecognized.

*Cormac McCarthy is best known to the world as a writer of novels. These include* Blood Meridian, All the Pretty Horses, No Country for Old Men, *and* The Road. *At the Santa Fe Institute (SFI) he is a research colleague and thought of in complementary terms. An aficionado on subjects ranging from the history of mathematics, philosophical arguments relating to the status of quantum mechanics as a causal theory, comparative evidence bearing on non-human intelligence, and the nature of the conscious and unconscious mind. At SFI we have been searching for the expression of these scientific interests in his novels and we maintain a furtive tally of their covert manifestations and demonstrations in his prose.*

*Over the last two decades Cormac and I have been discussing the puzzles and paradoxes of the unconscious mind. Foremost among them, the fact that the very recent and “uniquely” human capability of near infinite expressive power arising through a combinatorial grammar is built on the foundations of a far more ancient animal brain. How have these two evolutionary systems become reconciled? Cormac expresses this tension as the deep suspicion, perhaps even contempt, that the primeval unconscious feels toward the upstart, conscious language. In this article Cormac explores this idea through processes of dream and infection. It is a discerning and wide-ranging exploration of ideas and challenges that our research community has only recently dared to start addressing through complexity science.*

*—David Krakauer 
President and William H. Miller Professor of Complex Systems, Santa Fe Institute*

![https://lede-admin.nautil.us/wp-content/uploads/sites/70/12165_2b1a9e41c7cb15669337c1a583af31f8.png](https://lede-admin.nautil.us/wp-content/uploads/sites/70/12165_2b1a9e41c7cb15669337c1a583af31f8.png "SHA-256: 98865192887d0eb8bd3cd88f28929f26c7d867849a8615d267ea3cbc87fce882")

I call it the Kekulé Problem because among the myriad instances of scientific problems solved in the sleep of the inquirer Kekulé’s is probably the best known. He was trying to arrive at the configuration of the benzene molecule and not making much progress when he fell asleep in front of the fire and had his famous dream of a snake coiled in a hoop with its tail in its mouth—the ouroboros of mythology—and woke exclaiming to himself: “It’s a ring. The molecule is in the form of a ring.” Well. The problem of course—not Kekulé’s but ours—is that since the unconscious understands language perfectly well or it would not understand the problem in the first place, why doesnt it simply answer Kekulé’s question with something like: “Kekulé, it’s a bloody ring.” To which our scientist might respond: “Okay. Got it. Thanks.”

Why the snake? That is, why is the unconscious so loathe to speak to us? Why the images, metaphors, pictures? Why the dreams, for that matter.

A logical place to begin would be to define what the unconscious is in the first place. To do this we have to set aside the jargon of modern psychology and get back to biology. The unconscious is a biological system before it is anything else. To put it as pithily as possibly—and as accurately—the unconscious is a machine for operating an animal.

All animals have an unconscious. If they didnt they would be plants. We may sometimes credit ours with duties it doesnt actually perform. Systems at a certain level of necessity may require their own mechanics of governance. Breathing, for instance, is not controlled by the unconscious but by the pons and the medulla oblongata, two systems located in the brainstem. Except of course in the case of cetaceans, who have to breathe when they come up for air. An autonomous system wouldnt work here. The first dolphin anesthetized on an operating table simply died. (How do they sleep? With half of their brain alternately.) But the duties of the unconscious are beyond counting. Everything from scratching an itch to solving math problems.

> Did language meet some need? No. The other five thousand plus mammals among us do fine without it.

Problems in general are often well posed in terms of language and language remains a handy tool for explaining them. But the actual process of thinking—in any discipline—is largely an unconscious affair. Language can be used to sum up some point at which one has arrived—a sort of milepost—so as to gain a fresh starting point. But if you believe that you actually use language in the solving of problems I wish that you would write to me and tell me how you go about it.

I’ve pointed out to some of my mathematical friends that the unconscious appears to be better at math than they are. My friend George Zweig calls this the Night Shift. Bear in mind that the unconscious has no pencil or notepad and certainly no eraser. That it does solve problems in mathematics is indisputable. How does it go about it? When I’ve suggested to my friends that it may well do it without using numbers, most of them thought—after a while—that this was a possibility. How, we dont know. Just as we dont know how it is that we manage to talk. If I am talking to you then I can hardly be crafting at the same time the sentences that are to follow what I am now saying. I am totally occupied in talking to you. Nor can some part of my mind be assembling these sentences and then saying them to me so that I can repeat them. Aside from the fact that I am busy this would be to evoke an endless regress. The truth is that there is a process here to which we have no access. It is a mystery opaque to total blackness.

There are influential persons among us—of whom a bit more a bit later—who claim to believe that language is a totally evolutionary process. That it has somehow appeared in the brain in a primitive form and then grown to usefulness. Somewhat like vision, perhaps. But vision we now know is traceable to perhaps as many as a dozen quite independent evolutionary histories. Tempting material for the teleologists. These stories apparently begin with a crude organ capable of perceiving light where any occlusion could well suggest a predator. Which actually makes it an excellent scenario for Darwinian selection. It may be that the influential persons imagine all mammals waiting for language to appear. I dont know. But all indications are that language has appeared only once and in one species only. Among whom it then spread with considerable speed.

There are a number of examples of signaling in the animal world that might be taken for a proto-language. Chipmunks—among other species—have one alarm-call for aerial predators and another for those on the ground. Hawks as distinct from foxes or cats. Very useful. But what is missing here is the central idea of language—that one thing can be another thing. It is the idea that Helen Keller suddenly understood at the well. That the sign for water was not simply what you did to get a glass of water. It was the glass of water. It was in fact the water in the glass. This in the play *The Miracle Worker*. Not a dry eye in the house.

The invention of language was understood at once to be incredibly useful. Again, it seems to have spread through the species almost instantaneously. The immediate problem would seem to have been that there were more things to name than sounds to name them with. Language appears to have originated in southwestern Africa and it may even be that the clicks in the Khoisan languages—to include Sandawe and Hadza—are an atavistic remnant of addressing this need for a greater variety of sounds. The vocal problems were eventually handled evolutionarily—and apparently in fairly short order—by turning our throat over largely to the manufacture of speech.

## Overview

God has spoken, and continues to speak, through His Word, the Bible. Scripture points to Jesus, the source of life, restoration and salvation. **Yet 1 in 5 people around the world still do not have access** to the full Bible in a language and form they clearly understand.

Bible translation allows people everywhere to meaningfully engage with the Word. God speaks through Scripture to transform lives in every culture, whether it is shared in written form, sign language, oral Bible storytelling, audio or video.

## Your partnership is key

Your gift to the **Bible Translation Projects Fund** ensures that critical needs can be met quickly and effectively so more people can encounter God’s Word without delay. You can give with confidence knowing your support is helping advance translation work where it is needed most, right when it is needed.

items.body_excerpt:
[Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christians "Christians") leaders have written about male [homosexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexual "Homosexual") activities since the [first decades of Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Age "Apostolic Age"); female homosexual behavior was almost entirely ignored.[^1] Throughout the majority of [Christian history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Christianity "History of Christianity"), most [Christian theologians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_theology "Christian theology") and [denominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_denominations "Christian denominations") have considered homosexual behavior as [immoral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immoral "Immoral") or [sinful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin_in_Christianity "Sin in Christianity").[^2] [^3] [^4] [^5]

However, since the second half of the 20th century some prominent Christian theologians and religious groups have espoused a wide variety of beliefs and practices towards homosexuals, including the establishment of various "open and accepting" [Christian churches and denominations that actively support LGBT members](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT-affirming_Christian_denominations "LGBT-affirming Christian denominations").

## Etymology

The first instance of the English word "homosexuals" used in a biblical translation was in the [RSV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revised_Standard_Version "Revised Standard Version") New Testament published from 1946 until 1970,[^6] which simultaneously removed most "fornication" admonitions found in the prior [ASV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Standard_Version "American Standard Version") (1901) and [KJV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_James_Version "King James Version") (1611) [Bibles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible "Bible").[^7] Historically, the [Vulgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulgate "Vulgate") contains the Latin stem "fornicat" within 92 verses [^8] representing sixteen centuries of Christian tradition on literally wording sexual admonishments, while verses now rebuking homosexuals were described in the Vulgate equivalent to "male-prostitute male-concubines".[^9] RSV set a modern trend in literally rebuking "homosexuals".

Several [post-World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aftermath_of_World_War_II "Aftermath of World War II") translations of the Bible now have one to four verses rebuking homosexuals while replacing all mention of fornicators with "the immoral" or "sexual immoral" and leaving ambiguous homosexual or heterosexual immorality.[^10] [^11]

## Early Christianity

The history of Christianity and homosexuality has been much debated.[^12] The [Hebrew Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bible_and_homosexuality "The Bible and homosexuality") and its traditional interpretations in [Judaism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism "Judaism") and [Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") have historically affirmed and endorsed a [patriarchal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriarchy "Patriarchy") and [heteronormative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heteronormativity "Heteronormativity") approach towards [human sexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sexuality "Human sexuality"),[^13] [^14] favouring exclusively [penetrative vaginal intercourse between men and women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterosexual_intercourse "Heterosexual intercourse") within the boundaries of [marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") over all other forms of [human sexual activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sexual_activity "Human sexual activity"),[^13] [^14] including [autoeroticism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autoeroticism "Autoeroticism"), [masturbation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masturbation "Masturbation"), [oral sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_sex "Oral sex"), [non-penetrative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-penetrative_sex "Non-penetrative sex") and [non-heterosexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexual_sexual_practices "Homosexual sexual practices") sexual intercourse (all of which have been labeled as " [sodomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodomy "Sodomy") " by some at various times),[^15] believing and teaching that such behaviors are forbidden because they are considered [sinful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin_in_Christianity "Sin in Christianity"),[^13] [^14] and further compared to or derived from the behavior of the alleged residents of [Sodom and Gomorrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodom_and_Gomorrah "Sodom and Gomorrah").[^2] [^13] However, the status of LGBT people in [early Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Christianity "Early Christianity") is debated.[^12] [^16] [^17] Some maintain that the [early Christian churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Christianity "Early Christianity") deplored [transgender people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") and [same-sex relationships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_relationships "Same-sex relationships"), while others maintain that they accepted them on the level of their heterosexual counterparts. These disagreements concern, in some cases, the translations of certain terms, or the meaning and context of some [biblical passages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible "Bible").[^2]

Before the [rise of Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origins_of_Christianity "Origins of Christianity"), certain sexual practices that are today considered "homosexual" [^18] had existed among certain groups, with some degree of social acceptance in [ancient Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality_in_ancient_Rome "Homosexuality in ancient Rome") (e.g. the relationship of a Roman citizen with a slave). Both societies viewed [anal sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anal_sex "Anal sex") as an act of dominance by the [active (penetrating) partner over the passive (penetrated) partner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top,_bottom_and_versatile "Top, bottom and versatile"), representing no distinction from how [vaginal sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaginal_sex "Vaginal sex") was viewed. It was considered a sign of weakness and low social status (such as slavery or *[infamia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infamia "Infamia")*) for a man to assume the passive role. There was no such stigma against a man who assumed the active role.[^19] [^20] [^21] [Derrick Sherwin Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Sherwin_Bailey "Derrick Sherwin Bailey") and [Sarah Ruden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Ruden "Sarah Ruden") both caution that it is anachronistic to project modern understandings of homosexuality onto ancient writings.[^22] [^23]

The [Judaic prohibitions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/613_mitzvot "613 mitzvot") found in [Leviticus 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leviticus_18 "Leviticus 18"):22 and 20:13 address the issue of sex between two men. The latter verse (20:13) says: "And if a man also lies with mankind, as with womankind, both of them have committed [abomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abomination_\(Bible\) "Abomination (Bible)"); they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them."

In his fourth homily on Romans,[^24] [John Chrysostom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Chrysostom "John Chrysostom") argued in the [fourth century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_in_the_4th_century "Christianity in the 4th century") that homosexual acts are worse than murder and so degrading that they constitute a kind of punishment in itself, and that enjoyment of such acts makes them worse, "for suppose I were to see a person running naked, with his body all besmeared with mire, and yet not covering himself, but exulting in it, I should not rejoice with him, but should rather bewail that he did not even perceive that he was doing shamefully." **James Douglas Muir Leno** ([/ ˈ l ɛ n oʊ /](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") [*LEN-oh*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born April 28, 1950) [^1] is an American television host, comedian, and writer. After doing stand-up comedy for years, Leno was chosen in 1992 to replace [Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Carson "Johnny Carson") as the host of [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") 's *[The Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show "The Tonight Show")*; Leno hosted *The Tonight Show* until September 2009 when [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O%27Brien "Conan O'Brien") took over as host and Leno started a primetime talk show, *[The Jay Leno Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Jay_Leno_Show "The Jay Leno Show")*, which aired weeknights at 10:00 p.m. [ET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"), also on NBC. O'Brien turned down NBC's offer to have Leno host a half hour monologue show before *The Tonight Show* to boost ratings amid reported viewership diminishing, which sparked the [2010 *Tonight Show* conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Tonight_Show_conflict "2010 Tonight Show conflict") that resulted in Leno's returning to hosting the show on March 1, 2010.[^2] He hosted his last episode of his second tenure on February 6, 2014. That year, he was inducted into the [Television Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_Hall_of_Fame "Television Hall of Fame").[^3] From 2014 to 2022, he hosted *[Jay Leno's Garage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Leno%27s_Garage "Jay Leno's Garage"),* and from 2021 to 2023, hosted the revival of *[You Bet Your Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Bet_Your_Life "You Bet Your Life")*.

Leno writes a regular column in *Popular Mechanics* showcasing his car collection and giving automotive advice. He also writes occasional "Motormouth" articles for *[The Sunday Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sunday_Times "The Sunday Times")*.

## Early life

Leno was born April 28, 1950, in [New Rochelle, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Rochelle,_New_York "New Rochelle, New York"). His homemaker mother, Catherine ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Muir; 1911–1993), was born in [Greenock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenock "Greenock"), Scotland, and came to the United States at age 11. His father, Angelo (1910–1994), was an insurance salesman born in New York to immigrants from [Flumeri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flumeri "Flumeri"), Campania, Italy. Leno grew up in [Andover, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andover,_Massachusetts "Andover, Massachusetts"), and graduated from [Andover High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andover_High_School_\(Massachusetts\) "Andover High School (Massachusetts)").[^4] He obtained a [bachelor's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor%27s_degree "Bachelor's degree") in [speech therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_therapy "Speech therapy") from [Emerson College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerson_College "Emerson College") in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"), where he started a comedy club in 1973.[^5] His older brother, Patrick (May 12, 1940 – October 6, 2002),[^6] was a [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War") veteran who became an attorney.

## Career

### Early career

Leno made his first appearance on *The Tonight Show* on March 2, 1977, performing a comedy routine.[^7] [^8] During the 1970s, he had minor roles in several television series and films, first in the 1976 episode "J.J. in Trouble" of *[Good Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Times "Good Times"),* and the same year in the pilot of *[Holmes & Yo-Yo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holmes_%26_Yo-Yo "Holmes & Yo-Yo")*. After an uncredited appearance in the 1977 film *[Fun with Dick and Jane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fun_with_Dick_and_Jane_\(1977_film\) "Fun with Dick and Jane (1977 film)")*, he played more prominent roles in 1978 in *[American Hot Wax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hot_Wax "American Hot Wax")* and *[Silver Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Bears "Silver Bears")*. His other appearances from that period include guest spots on the television shows *[One Day at a Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_at_a_Time_\(1975_TV_series\) "One Day at a Time (1975 TV series)")*, *[Alice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_\(American_TV_series\) "Alice (American TV series)")* and *[Laverne & Shirley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laverne_%26_Shirley "Laverne & Shirley")*. He had minor roles in the films *[Americathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americathon "Americathon")* (1979), and *[Polyester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyester_\(film\) "Polyester (film)")* (1981). His only starring film role was the 1989 direct-to-video *[Collision Course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collision_Course_\(1989_film\) "Collision Course (1989 film)")*, with [Pat Morita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Morita "Pat Morita"). He also appeared numerous times on *[Late Night with David Letterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Night_with_David_Letterman "Late Night with David Letterman")*.

He also appeared on three weeks of the short-lived [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") [game show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_show "Game show") *[Match Game-Hollywood Squares Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Match_Game-Hollywood_Squares_Hour "Match Game-Hollywood Squares Hour")* in 1983 and 1984.

### The Tonight Show

![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Jay_Leno_%281993%29_by_Alan_Light.jpg/250px-Jay_Leno_%281993%29_by_Alan_Light.jpg](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Jay_Leno_%281993%29_by_Alan_Light.jpg/250px-Jay_Leno_%281993%29_by_Alan_Light.jpg "SHA-256: a29e7435a2e31941c936d542f10e2c82a3223df3b8aa8157880d2510aea88583")

Leno in 1993, in the year after becoming host of The Tonight Show

Starting in 1986, Leno was a regular substitute host for [Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Carson "Johnny Carson") on *[The Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show "The Tonight Show")*. In 1992, he replaced Carson as host [^9] amid controversy with [David Letterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Letterman "David Letterman"), who had been hosting *Late Night with David Letterman* since 1982 (which aired after *The Tonight Show*), and whom many—including Carson himself—expected to be Carson's successor. The story of this turbulent transition became the basis of [a book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Shift_\(book\) "The Late Shift (book)") and [a movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Shift_\(film\) "The Late Shift (film)"). Leno continued to perform as a stand-up comedian throughout his *Tonight Show* tenure. In 1988, he received a contract extension with NBC itself.[^10] The July 1995 episode of *The Tonight Show* which featured an interview with [Hugh Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Grant "Hugh Grant") (who had been arrested for receiving oral sex in a public place from a prostitute) saw Leno rate higher than Letterman for the first time.[^11]

In 2004, Leno signed a contract extension with [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") to retain him as host of *The Tonight Show* until 2009.[^12] Later in 2004, [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O%27Brien "Conan O'Brien") signed a contract with NBC to become the show's host in 2009, replacing Leno at that time.[^13]

Layer 2 gaming sur Bitcoin. First is first.

items.title: BitNAT
items.summary:
name
BitNAT
description
Bitcoin Native Artifacts derived from real transactions in Bitcoin halving blocks.
protocol_version
1.0
rule
One BitNAT per real transaction in each Bitcoin halving block (heights divisible by 210000).
items.body_excerpt:
name
BitNAT
description
Bitcoin Native Artifacts derived from real transactions in Bitcoin halving blocks.
protocol_version
1.0
rule
One BitNAT per real transaction in each Bitcoin halving block (heights divisible by 210000). All traits, identifiers, and rarity scores are deterministically derived from on-chain Bitcoin data per whitepaper §4.
active_halvings
H1-H4 at launch; extends to H5 (~April 2028) and beyond as they occur.
whitepaper_url
https://bitnat.io/whitepaper
child_schema
nftId
string — canonical id, e.g. 'bitnaut_h1_210000_0'
halving
integer — 1, 2, 3, ...
halvingBlock
integer — 210000, 420000, ...
txIndex
integer — 0-based position in the halving block
fixtureTxid
string — the originating Bitcoin txid
feeSats
integer — original transaction fee in sats (§8.1 claim cost)
traits
string[] — derived per §4
rarityScore
integer — block-local, not global (§4 Deterministic Evaluation)
license
CC0 — BitNAT artifacts are derived from public on-chain data and dedicated to the public domain.

items.title: ***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***
items.summary:
***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

Social media has placed immense power in our hands.
But the question is not whether these tools are good or bad.
items.body_excerpt:
***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

Social media has placed immense power in our hands.
But the question is not whether these tools are good or bad. The question is whether we remain their masters—or become their servants.

***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

Many years ago, Fr. Isaac Atallah, a disciple of St. Paisios, was asked whether video players were a blessing or a curse. His answer was simple: "The device has an on/off switch. When it harms you, turn it off." 
The same principle applies today.

***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

The problem is not technology itself. The problem is our failure to cultivate discipline, self-control, and virtue in the use of technology.

***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

Social media often exposes what is already present within us. Anger becomes public. Hasty judgments are shared instantly. Rumors spread without verification. What is hidden in the heart quickly becomes visible online.

***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

One of the greatest dangers is the harm we inflict on others. A careless comment may be read by thousands. Even if we later repent, the damage may continue long after we have forgotten our words.

***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

The Christian life requires vigilance. Not everything deserves our attention. Not every rumor deserves our belief. Not every thought deserves a public response.

***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

St. Silouan considered excessive attention to the news an obstacle to pure prayer. How much more should we examine the endless stream of information that surrounds us today?

***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

Before opening your device: Pray. Ask the Holy Spirit to guide your thoughts. Use technology for what is good, useful, and beneficial to others.

***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

Try a simple experiment: Set aside one hour each day and live as though you own no electronic means of communication. You may discover a measure of peace you did not know you were missing.

***Metropolitan Saba Isper (@SabaIsper):***

The goal is not to abandon technology. The goal is to become a messenger of peace and joy rather than agitation and division.

items.body_excerpt:
**Gnosticism in modern times**, commonly known as **neo-Gnosticism**, includes a variety of contemporary religious movements, stemming from [Gnostic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gnosticism "Gnosticism") ideas and systems from ancient [Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire "Roman Empire") society. The root word, gnosis, means knowledge, originating in [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews "Jews") and [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") social environments in the first and second century A.D.

The [Mandaeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandaeans "Mandaeans") are an ancient Gnostic [ethnoreligious group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnoreligious_group "Ethnoreligious group") that have survived and are found today in Iran, Iraq and diaspora communities in North America, Western Europe and Australia.

The late 19th century saw the publication of popular sympathetic studies making use of recently rediscovered source materials. In this period there was also the revival of a Gnostic religious movement in France. The emergence of the [Nag Hammadi library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nag_Hammadi_library "Nag Hammadi library") in 1945 greatly increased the amount of source material available. Its translation from [Coptic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coptic_language "Coptic language") into English and other modern languages in 1977 resulted in a wide dissemination, which had observable influence on several modern figures and upon modern Western culture in general. This article attempts to summarize those modern figures and movements that have been influenced by Gnosticism, both prior and subsequent to the Nag Hammadi discovery.

A number of ecclesiastical bodies that identify as Gnostic have set up or re-founded since World War II as well, including the [Ecclesia Gnostica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecclesia_Gnostica "Ecclesia Gnostica"), [Johannite Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannite_Church "Johannite Church"), [Ecclesia Gnostica Catholica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecclesia_Gnostica_Catholica "Ecclesia Gnostica Catholica"), the Ecclesia Gnostica Mysterioum, the Thomasine Church,[^1] the Alexandrian Gnostic Church, the [Ecclesia Gnostica Apostolica Catholica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecclesia_Gnostica_Apostolica_Catholica "Ecclesia Gnostica Apostolica Catholica"), the Gnostic Catholic Union, Ecclesia Valentinaris Antiqua, the Cathari Church of Wales, and the North American College of Gnostic Bishops.[^2]

## Late 19th century

Source materials were discovered in the 18th century. In 1769, the [Bruce Codex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Codex "Bruce Codex") was brought to England from [Upper Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Egypt "Upper Egypt") by the Scottish traveller [James Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bruce "James Bruce"), and subsequently bequeathed to the care of the [Bodleian Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bodleian_Library "Bodleian Library"), Oxford. Sometime prior to 1785, the [Askew Codex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pistis_Sophia "Pistis Sophia") (a.k.a. *Pistis Sophia*) was bought by the British Museum from the heirs of Dr. [Anthony Askew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Askew "Anthony Askew"). The *Pistis Sophia* text and a Latin translation of the Askew Codex by Moritz G. Schwartze were published in 1851. Although discovered in 1896, the Coptic [Berlin Codex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Codex "Berlin Codex") (a.k.a. the Akhmim Codex) was not 'rediscovered' until the 20th century.

### Charles William King

[Charles William King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_William_King "Charles William King") was a British writer and collector of ancient [gemstones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemstone "Gemstone") with magical inscriptions. His collection was sold because of his failing eyesight, and was presented in 1881 to the [Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Museum_of_Art,_New_York "Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York"). King was recognized as one of the greatest authorities on gems at the time.[^3]

In *The Gnostics and their Remains* (1864, 1887 2nd ed.) King sets out to show that rather than being a Western heresy, the origins of Gnosticism are to be found in the East, specifically in [Buddhism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism"). This theory was embraced by [Helena Blavatsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helena_Blavatsky "Helena Blavatsky"), who argued that it was *plausible*, but rejected by [G. R. S. Mead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G._R._S._Mead "G. R. S. Mead"). According to Mead, King's work "lacks the thoroughness of the specialist." [^4]

### Madame Blavatsky

[Helena Petrovna Blavatsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helena_Petrovna_Blavatsky "Helena Petrovna Blavatsky"), co-founder of the [Theosophical Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theosophy_\(Blavatskian\) "Theosophy (Blavatskian)"), wrote extensively on Gnostic ideas. A compilation of her writings on Gnosticism is over 270 pages long.[^5] The first edition of King's *The Gnostics and Their Remains* was repeatedly cited as a source and quoted in *[Isis Unveiled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isis_Unveiled "Isis Unveiled")*.

### G. R. S. Mead

[G. R. S. Mead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G._R._S._Mead "G. R. S. Mead") became a member of Blavatsky's Theosophical Society in 1884. He left the teaching profession in 1889 to become Blavatsky's private secretary, which he was until her death in 1891. Mead's interest in Gnosticism was likely awakened by Blavatsky, who discussed it at length in *[Isis Unveiled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isis_Unveiled "Isis Unveiled")*.[^6]

In 1890–1891 Mead published a serial article on *Pistis Sophia* in [*Lucifer* magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucifer_\(magazine\) "Lucifer (magazine)"), the first English translation of that work. In an article in 1891, Mead argues for the recovery of the literature and thought of the West at a time when Theosophy was largely directed to the East, saying that this recovery of Western antique traditions is a work of interpretation and "the rendering of tardy justice to pagans and heretics, the reviled and rejected pioneers of progress..." [^7] This was the direction his own work was to take.

The first edition of his translation of *[Pistis Sophia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pistis_Sophia "Pistis Sophia")* appeared in 1896. From 1896 to 1898 Mead published another serial article in the same periodical, "Among the Gnostics of the First Two Centuries", that laid the foundation for his compendium *Fragments of a Faith Forgotten* in 1900. Mead serially published translations from the *[Corpus Hermeticum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_Hermeticum "Corpus Hermeticum")* from 1900 to 1905. The next year he published *Thrice-Greatest Hermes*, a comprehensive three-volume treatise. His series *Echoes of the Gnosis* was published in 12 booklets in 1908. By the time he left the Theosophical Society in 1909, he had published many influential translations, commentaries, and studies of ancient Gnostic texts. "Mead made Gnosticism accessible to the intelligent public outside of academia." [^8] Mead's work has had and continues to have widespread influence.[^9]

### Gnostic Church revival in France

After a series of visions and archival finds of [Cathar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathar "Cathar") -related documents, a librarian named Jules-Benoît Stanislas Doinel du Val-Michel (a.k.a. [Jules Doinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jules_Doinel "Jules Doinel")) established the *[Église Gnostique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gnostic_Church_of_France "Gnostic Church of France")* (French: *Gnostic Church*). Founded on extant Cathar documents with the Gospel of John and strong influence of [Simonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simonians "Simonians") and [Valentinian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/

items.body_excerpt:
**Anton Szandor LaVey** [^1] (born **Howard Stanton Levey**; April 11, 1930 – October 29, 1997) was an American writer, musician, and [Satanist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satanism "Satanism").[^2] He was the founder of the [Church of Satan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Satan "Church of Satan"), and the philosophy of [LaVeyan Satanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaVeyan_Satanism "LaVeyan Satanism"). He authored several books, including *[The Satanic Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Satanic_Bible "The Satanic Bible")*, *[The Satanic Witch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Satanic_Witch "The Satanic Witch")*, *[The Satanic Rituals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Satanic_Rituals "The Satanic Rituals")*, *[The Devil's Notebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Devil%27s_Notebook "The Devil's Notebook")*, and *[Satan Speaks!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satan_Speaks! "Satan Speaks!")*. In addition, he released three albums, including *[The Satanic Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Satanic_Mass "The Satanic Mass")*, *[Satan Takes a Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satan_Takes_a_Holiday "Satan Takes a Holiday")*, and *[Strange Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange_Music_\(album\) "Strange Music (album)")*. He played a minor on-screen role and served as technical advisor for the 1975 film *[The Devil's Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Devil%27s_Rain_\(film\) "The Devil's Rain (film)")* [^3] and served as host and narrator for [Nick Bougas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Bougas "Nick Bougas") ' 1989 [mondo film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mondo_film "Mondo film") *[Death Scenes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_Scenes "Death Scenes")*.[^4]

Historian of Satanism Gareth J. Medway described LaVey as a "born showman",[^5] with anthropologist [Jean La Fontaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_La_Fontaine "Jean La Fontaine") describing him as a "colourful figure of considerable personal magnetism".[^6] The academic scholars of Satanism Per Faxneld and Jesper Aagaard Petersen described LaVey as "the most iconic figure in the Satanic milieu".[^7] LaVey was labeled many things by journalists, religious detractors, and Satanists alike, including "The Father of Satanism",[^8] the " [St. Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_the_Apostle "Paul the Apostle") of Satanism",[^9] "The Black Pope",[^10] and the "evilest man in the world".[^1]

## Early life

LaVey was born Howard Stanton Levey on April 11, 1930 in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"), to an American family with mixed European ancestry. His parents were Michael Joseph Levey (1903–1992) and Gertrude Augusta ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Coulton). He later wrote confusing and contradictory accounts of his ancestry, for instance describing his maternal grandmother as a " [gypsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gypsy "Gypsy") " from [Transylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transylvania "Transylvania"), which was false, as she was born in [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine").[^11] The [hagiography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagiography "Hagiography") by LaVey's partner [Blanche Barton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanche_Barton "Blanche Barton") — *[The Secret Life of a Satanist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Secret_Life_of_a_Satanist "The Secret Life of a Satanist")* —describes his maternal grandmother as coming from a gypsy father and a Jewish mother from Transylvania.[^12] Barton merely interpreted LaVey's writings and did not research European birth records. LaVey was in fact born to Russian Jewish immigrants on both matrilineal and patrilineal sides.[^13]

His parents supported his musical interests, as he tried a number of instruments; his favorites were keyboards such as the [piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano "Piano") and [accordion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accordion "Accordion"). Anton played piano in a Baptist church as a boy, and played [oboe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oboe "Oboe") in high school.[^14] [^15] [^16]

He attended [Tamalpais High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamalpais_High_School "Tamalpais High School") in [Mill Valley, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mill_Valley,_California "Mill Valley, California"), until the age of 16.[^10] [^17] LaVey claimed he left high school at age 16 to join the [Clyde Beatty Circus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Beatty_Circus "Clyde Beatty Circus") and later [carnivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnival "Carnival"), first as a [roustabout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roustabout "Roustabout") and cage boy in an act with the big cats, then as a musician playing the [calliope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calliope_\(music\) "Calliope (music)").[^18] However, journalist [Lawrence Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Wright "Lawrence Wright") investigated LaVey's background and found no evidence LaVey ever worked in a circus either as a musician or a cage boy.[^1]

In the winter of 1948, LaVey began to work as an organist in bars, lounges, and nightclubs. His "genius" on keyboards helped him attain gigs.[^1] [^19] He claimed to have had a brief affair with then-unknown [Marilyn Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Monroe "Marilyn Monroe") while playing organ in Los Angeles [burlesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_burlesque "American burlesque") houses, stating that she was a dancer at the [Mayan Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayan_Theater "Mayan Theater") at the time. This was challenged by those who knew Monroe then, as well as the manager of the Mayan, Paul Valentine, who said she had never been one of his dancers, nor had the theater ever been used as a burlesque house.[^20]

According to his biography, LaVey moved back to San Francisco. LaVey met Carole Lansing in 1950, and they married the following year, when Lansing was fifteen years old. Lansing gave birth to LaVey's first daughter, [Karla LaVey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_LaVey "Karla LaVey"), born in 1952. In order to avoid the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") draft, he studied criminology at the [City College of San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_College_of_San_Francisco "City College of San Francisco"). LaVey then attained a job as a photographer for the [San Francisco Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Police_Department "San Francisco Police Department") (SFPD),[^1] where he worked for three years. (Wright could find no evidence of LaVey being enrolled at the City College of San Francisco or working at this job either.) [^21] LaVey claimed to have dabbled as a [psychic investigator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychic_investigator "Psychic investigator"), looking into "800 calls" referred to him by SFPD. Later biographers questioned whether LaVey ever worked with the SFPD, as there are no records substantiating the claim.[^1] [^22]

LaVey and Carole divorced in 1960, after LaVey became involved with [Diane Hegarty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Hegarty "Diane Hegarty"). Hegarty and LaVey never married, but she was his companion for 24 years and mothered his second daughter, [Zeena Galatea Schreck (*née* LaVey)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeena_Schreck "Zeena Schreck") (born in 1963).[^23] At the end of their relationship, Hegarty sued for [palimony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palimony "Palimony").[^24] [^25]

## Church of Satan

Anton Lavey became a local celebrity in San Francisco through his [paranormal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paranormal "Paranormal") research and live performances as an organist, including playing the [Wurlitzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wurlitzer "Wurlitzer") at the Lost Weekend cocktail lounge.[^26] He was also a publicly noticeable figure

Some varieties of atheism on left Implicit " negative " / " weak soft " atheists who lack a belief in gods without explicitly denying the concept, includes very young children, those who are unacquainted with the concept or are truly undecided. on right Explicit " atheists who do not believe that gods exist necessarily. positive strong hard " atheists who firmly believe that gods do not exist. Note: Areas in the diagram are not meant to indicate relative numbers of people.

**Implicit atheism** and **explicit atheism** are types of [atheism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheism "Atheism").[^1] In [George H. Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._Smith "George H. Smith") 's *Atheism: The Case Against God*, "implicit atheism" is defined as "the absence of theistic belief without a conscious rejection of it", while "explicit atheism" is "the absence of theistic belief due to a conscious rejection of it".[^1] Explicit atheists have considered the idea of [deities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deity "Deity") and have rejected belief that any exist. Implicit atheists, though they do not themselves maintain a belief in a god or gods, have not rejected the notion or have not considered it further.

## Implicit atheism

"Implicit atheism" is "the absence of theistic belief without a conscious rejection of it". "Absence of theistic belief" encompasses all forms of non-belief in deities. This would categorize as implicit atheists those adults who have never heard of the concept of deities, and those adults who have not given the idea any real consideration. Also included are agnostics who assert they do not believe in any deities (even if they claim not to be atheists), and children. As far back as 1772, [Baron d'Holbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baron_d%27Holbach "Baron d'Holbach") said that "All children are born Atheists; they have no idea of God".[^2] Smith is silent on newborn children, but clearly identifies as atheists some children who are unaware of any concept of any deity:

> The man who is unacquainted with theism is an atheist because he does not believe in a god. This category would also include the child with the conceptual capacity to grasp the issues involved, but who is still unaware of those issues. The fact that this child does not believe in god qualifies him as an atheist.[^1]

## Explicit atheism

Smith observes that some motivations for explicit atheism are rational and some not. Of the rational motivations, he says:

> The most significant variety of atheism is explicit atheism of a philosophical nature. This atheism contends that the belief in god is irrational and should therefore be rejected. Since this version of explicit atheism rests on a criticism of theistic beliefs, it is best described as *critical atheism*.[^1]

For Smith, critical, explicit atheism is subdivided further into three groups:[^1] <sup>p.17</sup>

1. the view usually expressed by the statement "I do not believe in the existence of a god or supernatural being" after "the failure of theism to provide sufficient evidence in its favor. Faced with a lack of evidence, this explicit atheist sees no reason whatsoever for believing in a supernatural being";
2. the view usually expressed by the statement "God does not exist" or "the existence of God is impossible" after "a particular concept of god, such as the God of Christianity, is judged to be absurd or contradictory";
3. the view which "refuses to discuss the existence or nonexistence of a god" because "the concept of a 'god' is unintelligible".

For the purposes of his paper on "philosophical atheism", [Ernest Nagel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_Nagel "Ernest Nagel") chose to attach only the explicit atheism definition for his examination and discussion:

> I must begin by stating what sense I am attaching to the word "atheism," and how I am construing the theme of this paper. I shall understand by "atheism" a critique and a denial of the major claims of all varieties of theism. \[...\] atheism is not to be identified with sheer unbelief, or with disbelief in some particular creed of a religious group. Thus, a child who has received no religious instruction and has never heard about God, is not an atheist – for he is not denying any theistic claims. Similarly in the case of an adult who, if he has withdrawn from the faith of his father without reflection or because of frank indifference to any theological issue, is also not an atheist – for such an adult is not challenging theism and not professing any views on the subject. \[...\] I propose to examine some *philosophic* concepts of atheism...[^3]

In Nagel's *Philosophical Concepts of Atheism*, he very much agrees with Smith on the three-part subdivision of "explicit atheism" above, though Nagel does not use the term "explicit".

## Other typologies of atheism

The specific narrow focus on [positive atheism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negative_and_positive_atheism "Negative and positive atheism") taken by some professional philosophers like Nagel on the one hand, compared with the scholarship on traditional negative atheism of freethinkers like [d'Holbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baron_d%27Holbach "Baron d'Holbach") and Smith on the other has been attributed to the different concerns of professional philosophers and layman proponents of atheism,

> "If so many atheists and some of their critics have insisted on the negative definition of atheism, why have some modern philosophers called for a positive definition of atheism – atheism as the outright denial of God's existence? Part of the reason, I suspect, lies in the chasm separating freethinkers and academic philosophers. Most modern philosophers are totally unfamiliar with atheistic literature and so remain oblivious to the tradition of negative atheism contained in that literature. (see Smith (1990, Chapter 3, p. 51–60 [^4]))

Everitt (2004) makes the point that professional philosophers are more interested in the grounds for giving or withholding assent to propositions:

> We need to distinguish between a *biographical* or *sociological* enquiry into why some people have believed or disbelieved in God, and an *[epistemological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistemological "Epistemological")* enquiry into whether there are any good reasons for either belief or unbelief... We are interested in the question of what *good reasons* there are for or against God's existence, and no light is thrown on that question by discovering people who hold their beliefs without having good reasons for them.[^5]

So, sometimes in philosophy (Flew, Martin and Nagel notwithstanding), only the explicit "denial of theistic belief" is examined, rather than the broader, implicit subject of atheism.

The terms ["weak atheism" and "strong atheism"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weak_and_strong_atheism "Weak and strong atheism"), also known as "negative atheism" and "positive atheism", are usually used by Smith as synonyms of the less well-known "implicit" and "explicit" categories. "Strong explicit" atheists assert that it is false that any deities exist. "Weak explicit" atheists assert they do not believe in deities, and do not assert it is *true* that deities do not exist. Those who do not believe any deities exist, and do not assert their non-belief are included among implicit atheists. Among weak implicit atheists are included the following: children and adults who have never heard of deities; people who have heard of deities but have never given the idea any considerable thought; and those agnostics who suspend belief about deities, but do not reject such belief.[^1]

**Volodymyr Katriuk** (1 October 1921 – 22 May 2015) was a Ukrainian-Canadian soldier and beekeeper, who was accused of having taken part in the [Khatyn massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khatyn_massacre "Khatyn massacre") and other massacres under the cover of [anti-partisan warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-partisan_warfare "Anti-partisan warfare") as a member of the [Schutzmannschaft Battalion 118](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schutzmannschaft_Battalion_118 "Schutzmannschaft Battalion 118") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[^1] [^2] In the annual Nazi War Criminal Report for the years 2012, 2013 and 2014, Katriuk was ranked number three under the [list of most-wanted Nazi war criminals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-wanted_Nazi_war_criminals "List of most-wanted Nazi war criminals") as determined by the [Simon Wiesenthal Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Wiesenthal_Center "Simon Wiesenthal Center").[^2] Katriuk denied any involvement in [war crimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_crime "War crime").[^2] [^3] On 18 March 2024, the [Supreme Court of Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Belarus "Supreme Court of Belarus") ruled that Katriuk was guilty of the "genocide of the [Belarusian people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarusian_people "Belarusian people") ".[^1]

## Early life

Katriuk was born in the village of [Luzhany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzhany "Luzhany"), near the city of [Chernivtsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chernivtsi "Chernivtsi"), on 1 October 1921. Chernivtsi is situated in the [Bukovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukovina "Bukovina") region, which was then part of the [Kingdom of Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Romania "Kingdom of Romania").

## Second World War

In 1942 Katriuk joined [*Schutzmannschaft* Battalion 118](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schutzmannschaft_Batallion_118 "Schutzmannschaft Batallion 118") to fight the [Soviet partisans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_partisans "Soviet partisans"). Katriuk's Nazi ties were known at the time of a 1999 Federal Court of Canada decision, but more details did not emerge until the release in 2008 of KGB [interrogation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interrogation "Interrogation") reports at the trial of [Hryhoriy Vasiura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hryhoriy_Vasiura "Hryhoriy Vasiura"), one of the battalion officers.[^4] The new KGB documents, yet unseen by the general public, claim that Katriuk was directly involved in the [Khatyn massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khatyn_massacre "Khatyn massacre").[^2]

In an article published in *Holocaust and Genocide Studies*,[^5] [Lund University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lund_University "Lund University") historian [Per Anders Rudling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_Anders_Rudling "Per Anders Rudling"), relying on new KGB interrogation reports, wrote that "One witness stated that Volodymyr Katriuk was a particularly active participant in the atrocity: he reportedly lay behind the stationary [machine gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MG_42 "MG 42"), firing rounds on anyone attempting to escape the flames." [^2] Rudling also said that Katriuk was "an active participant in the ‘pacification’ of the [Jewish partisans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_partisans "Jewish partisans") of the [Naliboki forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naliboki_forest "Naliboki forest") ".[^6]

Another Soviet war crimes trial in 1973 heard that Katriuk and two others killed a group of Belarusian loggers earlier on that day, suspecting they were part of a popular uprising. "I saw how Ivankiv was firing with a machine gun upon the people who were running for cover in the forest, and how Katriuk and [Meleshko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasyl_Meleshko "Vasyl Meleshko") were shooting the people lying on the road," the witness said.[^4] Katriuk was a member of [Schutzmannschaft Battalion 118](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schutzmannschaft_Battalion_118 "Schutzmannschaft Battalion 118") that helped the [Nazis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") to create "dead zones." [^4] The dead zone policy involved exterminating Soviet partisans who had launched ambushes against Nazi forces.[^4]

### Double defection

Katriuk claimed in Federal Court that in August 1944 he defected with the entire battalion and joined the [French Resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Resistance "French Resistance") to fight the Nazis. Later that year he was transferred to the [French Foreign Legion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Foreign_Legion "French Foreign Legion"),[^7] as a private, and was one of twenty to twenty-five volunteers who were dispatched by their French commanders to go to the front to fight the German army. Katriuk was placed in charge of a machine gun and, during the course of his service, was severely injured.[^8]

He spent two and a half months in an American hospital in France.[^8] Katriuk claimed to have fought later at the Italian front near [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco") until the end of World War II.[^8] He remained in the Foreign Legion to avoid repatriation, but soon learned that his unit would be sent to fight in [Indochina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Indochina "French Indochina"), to which his commanding officer, whom he had a poor relationship with, said that Katriuk would be unlikely to survive.[^8] Katriuk deserted while on leave in July 1945, obtained false identity papers with a new birthday, under the name of his brother-in-law, and got a job in a butcher shop in Paris.[^9]

## Later life

In 1951, Katriuk immigrated to [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada") from [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"). In 1959, he became a [beekeeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beekeeper "Beekeeper") in [Ormstown, Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ormstown,_Quebec "Ormstown, Quebec"), where he owned a [beekeeping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beekeeping "Beekeeping") [farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farm "Farm") and lived in a small house on the property with his wife Maria.[^2] [^9]

### Canadian citizenship question

In August 1996, Katriuk was notified that the Canadian government was seeking to revoke his citizenship. The decision was to be made by the [Cabinet of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Canada "Cabinet of Canada").[^9] In 1999, a [Federal Court of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Court_of_Canada "Federal Court of Canada") decision concluded that Katriuk immigrated to the country under a [pseudonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym") and obtained his [Canadian citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_nationality_law "Canadian nationality law") by providing false information.[^10] [^2] However, the court found no evidence that Katriuk had participated in war crimes,[^10] and in 2007, the cabinet halted revocation proceedings.[^2] [^11] In 2012, the Canadian government pledged to re-examine the case, although this did not occur.[^11]

### Death

Katriuk died of a stroke in a hospital in [Salaberry-de-Valleyfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salaberry-de-Valleyfield "Salaberry-de-Valleyfield"), Quebec on 22 May 2015 at the age of 93.[^6] Two weeks before his death, the [Investigative Committee of Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investigative_Committee_of_Russia "Investigative Committee of Russia") called on Canada to deport Katriuk to the [Russian Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Federation "Russian Federation") so he could stand trial, according to international law; the Canadian government, whose relations with the Russian government have been strained since the [2014 Russian annexation of Crimea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Russian_annexation_of_Crimea "2014 Russian annexation of Crime

**Dawson College** is an [English-language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_English "Quebec English") [public college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_college "Public college") in [Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal,_Quebec "Montreal, Quebec"), [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec"), [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"). The college is situated near the heart of [Downtown Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Montreal "Downtown Montreal") in a former nunnery on approximately 12 acres (5 ha) of green space. It is the largest [CEGEP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEGEP "CEGEP") in the province of Quebec, with a student population of approximately 8,000 day students and 3,000 evening students enrolled in more than 30 fields of study.[^1]

## History

![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Dawson_College_1.jpg/250px-Dawson_College_1.jpg](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Dawson_College_1.jpg/250px-Dawson_College_1.jpg "SHA-256: 2188befe200d31d3bbc355f341d5c803a4e82a93e1647cefc7d508d01f59b5d0")

Dawson College in 2025

In September 1945, [McGill University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McGill_University "McGill University") established a satellite campus called Sir William Dawson College at the [Royal Canadian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Canadian_Air_Force "Royal Canadian Air Force") base in St. Johns (now [Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu "Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu")), Quebec. This first incarnation of the college was set up to handle the overflow registration of servicemen after the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"). Populated mainly by engineering and science students who were required to live onsite, the college operated for five years.[^2] It was named after [Sir William Dawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_William_Dawson "John William Dawson"), a principal of McGill University from 1855 to 1893.

After the General Vocational College Act came into effect in June 1967, Dawson College became the first English-language institution in the new CEGEP network. It opened its doors in September 1969 to 1,655 students. The college was originally housed in a converted pharmaceutical factory at 350 Selby Street in [Westmount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westmount "Westmount"). In 1970, a second campus, used mostly for Creative Arts programs, was opened on Viger Street just to the north of [Old Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Montreal "Old Montreal"). During the next few years, additional spaces were rented across the city such as 4333 Ste. Catherine St. W. (Data Processing, Continuing Education), the Show Mart at Berri (gym), Dome Theatre on Notre Dame St., the Richelieu Building at 990 du Couvent and the La Fontaine building on Sherbrooke Street East. Finally, in 1975, the Victoria Campus was added at 485 [McGill St.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McGill_Street_\(Montreal\) "McGill Street (Montreal)")

In August 1982, the college signed an agreement to acquire the Mother House of the Sisters of the [Congrégation de Notre-Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregation_of_Notre_Dame_of_Montreal "Congregation of Notre Dame of Montreal") in order to unify its fourteen separate locations.[^3] The campus opened in 1988, and consolidation happened in 1997 when the Selby Campus was closed.

In August 2010, because of an increase in CEGEP enrollments, the college was faced again with a lack of space. The fourth floor of the [Pepsi Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepsi_Forum "Pepsi Forum") on [Atwater Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atwater_Street "Atwater Street") was leased, allowing for the addition of new classrooms.[^4] The [P Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepsi_Forum "Pepsi Forum") is equipped with six classrooms for regular day [DEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_Diploma_of_College_Studies "Quebec Diploma of College Studies") students and one classroom and a computer laboratory for [AEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEGEP "CEGEP") students. A security office and student lounge were also added. In 2011, an additional 4 rooms were added to the 4th floor for general study. In 2018, Dawson leased additional space on the Forum 2nd floor, adding general classrooms, active learning rooms and 4 labs for the college Physiotherapy Technology Program.

In 2020, the college was awarded the gold rating for leadership in sustainability by [The Sustainability Tracking, Assessment & Rating System (STARS)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_for_the_Advancement_of_Sustainability_in_Higher_Education#STARS "Association for the Advancement of Sustainability in Higher Education").[^5] The college's initiatives include, among other things, a pledge to [carbon neutrality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_neutrality "Carbon neutrality"), rooftop gardens, certificate programs in Sustainable Happiness, and a student-led initiative to compost waste.[^6] [^7]

## Programs

![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Dawson_College_04.jpg/250px-Dawson_College_04.jpg](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Dawson_College_04.jpg/250px-Dawson_College_04.jpg "SHA-256: 8e3d0c35dc00618a2ebdcad2660b3ce614f4aab5bd7c76afe5e2b7caa782476a")

The de Maisonneuve entrance of Dawson College

The CEGEP offers two types of programs: pre-university and career/technical. Pre-university programs take two years to complete and cover subject matter that roughly corresponds to the additional year of high school given elsewhere in Canada, as well as university-level introductory courses that prepare students for their chosen field in university. Technical programs take three years to complete and allow graduates to enter the workforce or to pursue their studies at a university level.

Evening courses are offered through continuing education in both credit and non-credit divisions. Corporate training is available as well.

### Pre-university programs

- Creative & Applied Arts
 - Arts, Literature and Communication (ALC)
 - Arts and Culture
 - Cinema-Communications
 - Interactive Media Arts
 - Languages
 - Literature
 - Studio Arts
 - Visual Arts
- Science, Medical Studies & Engineering
 - Science
 - Pure and Applied Science
 - Health Science
 - Enriched Science (formerly known as First Choice Science)
 - Enriched Pure and Applied Science
 - Enriched Health Science
 - Environmental Science
 - Explorations Science
 - Developmental Science
 - Science, Computer Science, and Mathematics
- Social Science & Business Technologies
 - Social Science
 - General Social Science
 - Commerce
 - Child Studies
 - Environmental Studies
 - International Business Studies
 - Law, Society and Justice
 - Social Change and Solidarity (similar to former North-South Studies)
 - Psychology
 - Travel and Tourism
 - Liberal Arts

Pre-university programs usually require four semesters (two years) to complete.

#### Enriched Science

Formerly named First Choice Science, Dawson College's honours science program is known as Enriched Science. Enrolled students can choose between the Pure and Applied Science or the Health Science profiles.[^8]

### Career/technical programs

- Creative & Applied Arts
 - 3D Animation and Computer Generated Imagery
 - Graphic Design
 - Illustration
 - Industrial Design
 - Interior Design
 - Professional Photography
 - Professional Theatre
- Science, Medical Studies, and Engineering
 - Biomedical Laboratory Technology
 - Civil Engineering Technology
 - Diagnostic Imaging
 - Electrical Engineering Technology
 - Laboratory Technology – Analytical Chemistry
 - Mechanical Engineering Technology
 - Nursing
 - Physiotherapy Technology
 - Radiation Oncology
- Social Science and Business Technology
 - Accounting and Management Technology
 - Business Management (Marketing)
 - Community Recreation and Leader

$Host.UI.RawUI.BackgroundColor = "Black"

# Set text color

# Define commands and their descriptions
$adbCommands = @(

@{ "Description" = "List all connected devices"; "Command" = "adb devices" }

 
 
@{ "Description" = "Get device IP address"; "Command" = "adb shell ip route | Select-String -Pattern 'src ([0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3})' | ForEach-Object { `$_.Matches.Groups[1].Value }" }

 
@{ "Description" = "Connect headset to wireless"; "Command" = "adb tcpip 5555; Start-Sleep -s 3; `$ips = @(adb shell ip route | Select-String -Pattern 'src ([0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3})' | ForEach-Object { `$_.Matches.Groups[1].Value }); Write-Output `$ips; if (`$ips.Count -gt 0) { adb connect ('{0}:5555' -f `$ips[0].Trim()) } else { Write-Output 'Could not determine device IP address.' }" }

@{ "Description" = "Disconnect headset from wireless"; "Command" = "adb tcpip 5555; Start-Sleep -s 3; `$ips = @(adb shell ip route | Select-String -Pattern 'src ([0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3})' | ForEach-Object { `$_.Matches.Groups[1].Value }); Write-Output `$ips; if (`$ips.Count -gt 0) { adb disconnect ('{0}:5555' -f `$ips[0].Trim()) } else { Write-Output 'Could not determine device IP address.' }" }

 
@{ "Description" = "Install base.apk"; "Command" = "adb install base.apk" }

 
@{ "Description" = "List all third party packages"; "Command" = "adb shell cmd package list packages -3" }
 

 
@{ "Description" = "Get app version number"; "Command" = "`$packageName = Read-Host 'Enter package name'; (adb shell dumpsys package `$packageName | findstr versionCode) -replace '.*versionCode=([0-9]+).*', '`$1'" }

 
@{ "Description" = "Find package path"; "Command" = "`$packageName = Read-Host 'Enter package name'; adb shell pm path `$packageName" }
 
 

@{ "Description" = "base.apk file size check"; "Command" = "`$packageName = Read-Host 'Enter package name'; `$packagePath = (adb shell pm path `$packageName).Trim().Replace('package:', ''); `$output = adb shell du -m `$packagePath; `$output | ForEach-Object { `$_ -replace '`t', ' ' } | ForEach-Object { `$(`$_ -split ' ')[0] + ' MB ' + `$(`$_ -split ' ')[1] }" }

 
@{ "Description" = "Pull base.apk"; "Command" = "`$packageName = Read-Host 'Enter package name'; `$packagePath = (adb shell pm path `$packageName).Trim().Replace('package:', ''); adb pull `$packagePath" }

 
@{ "Description" = "Uninstall program"; "Command" = "`$packageName = Read-Host 'Enter package name'; adb uninstall `$packageName" }

 

@{ "Description" = "List OBB folders"; "Command" = "adb shell ls /storage/emulated/0/Android/obb/" }
 
 

@{ "Description" = "List OBB file sizes"; "Command" = "`$obbFolder = Read-Host 'Enter OBB folder name'; adb shell du -m /storage/emulated/0/Android/obb/`$obbFolder/* | ForEach-Object { `$_ -replace '`t', ' ' } | ForEach-Object { `$(`$_ -split ' ')[0] + ' MB ' + `$(`$_ -split ' ')[1] }" }
 
 

@{ "Description" = "Pull OBB folder"; "Command" = "`$obbFolder = Read-Host 'Enter OBB folder name'; adb pull /storage/emulated/0/Android/obb/`$obbFolder" }
 
 

@{ "Description" = "Push OBB folder"; "Command" = "`$obbFolder = Read-Host 'Enter OBB folder name'; adb shell mkdir -p /storage/emulated/0/Android/obb/`$obbFolder; adb push `$obbFolder/. /storage/emulated/0/Android/obb/`$obbFolder/" }

 
 
@
