# **The Metaweb Charter**

## **Draft Charter for Stewardship of the Meta-Layer Ecosystem**

# **Preamble**

Humanity is entering a new phase of planetary cognition.

The Internet has evolved from a network of documents into a shared cognitive environment that increasingly shapes perception, coordination, governance, culture, economics, and civilization itself.

Yet the current Web remains fragmented, extractive, and structurally limited in its ability to support collective intelligence, contextual trust, democratic coordination, and safe human–AI coexistence.

The Meta-Layer Guild exists to help steward the emergence of a new civic and cognitive layer above the webpage: an interoperable meta-layer that enables humanity to collaboratively build trustworthy digital environments, contextual knowledge systems, and shared coordination infrastructure.

The Guild recognizes the foundational contributions of Douglas Engelbart, whose vision of augmenting human intellect through collective systems remains unfinished, and Pierre Teilhard de Chardin, whose concept of the noosphere anticipated the emergence of a planetary layer of shared cognition.

The Guild views the meta-layer as part of the long arc of humanity’s cognitive evolution.

A digital noosphere.

A shared civic intelligence environment.

A coordination substrate through which humanity may learn to think together more wisely.

The Guild exists to help steward this emergence responsibly.

# **Article I: Purpose**

The Meta-Layer Guild exists to help steward the emergence of a trustworthy civic and cognitive layer above the webpage.

The Guild understands the meta-layer not merely as a technical stack, but as an evolving coordination environment through which humanity increasingly thinks, remembers, deliberates, learns, governs, and creates meaning together.

The purpose of the Guild is therefore both infrastructural and civilizational.

Practically, the Guild supports the development of interoperable overlay systems, trust architectures, governance frameworks, identity systems, contextual knowledge layers, and public-interest interface infrastructure.

Civically, the Guild seeks to strengthen humanity’s capacity for collective intelligence, democratic coordination, contextual trust, and regenerative cooperation in an age increasingly shaped by AI systems and planetary-scale interdependence.

The Guild exists to help ensure that the emerging meta-layer develops as a public-interest civic substrate rather than a proprietary enclosure controlled by narrow institutional or commercial interests.

The Guild therefore supports the cultivation of systems that strengthen collective intelligence, contextual trust, cognitive freedom, safe human–AI coexistence, composable governance, interoperable civic infrastructure, planetary coordination, and regenerative forms of digital civilization. These are not viewed as isolated objectives, but as deeply interconnected dimensions of a healthy civic meta-layer.

# **Article II: Foundational Orientation**

The Meta-Layer Guild begins from the recognition that digital infrastructure is no longer peripheral to civilization.

The Internet now functions as a primary cognitive environment that shapes perception, memory, governance, economics, social identity, institutional trust, and collective behavior.

Interfaces increasingly mediate how humanity understands reality itself.

This transition creates both extraordinary opportunity and unprecedented risk.

The same systems capable of enabling planetary collaboration can also amplify fragmentation, synthetic manipulation, epistemic instability, surveillance, and institutional breakdown.

The Guild therefore views the development of trustworthy interface infrastructure as a core civic challenge of the twenty-first century.

The Guild recognizes that collective intelligence does not emerge automatically from connectivity alone. Trust infrastructure, accountable governance, and meaningful contextual integrity are necessary conditions for democratic resilience in increasingly AI-mediated environments. Humanity now requires coordination systems capable of operating across cultures and planetary scale without collapsing into centralized control or epistemic fragmentation. The Guild therefore views cognitive freedom and public-interest interface infrastructure as essential civic concerns rather than optional technological features. No single institution, corporation, or state should possess unilateral authority over humanity’s shared cognitive infrastructure.

The Guild seeks to steward the emergence of a pluralistic, interoperable, democratically aligned meta-layer ecosystem capable of supporting human flourishing under conditions of increasing technological complexity.

# **Article III: Intellectual Foundations**

The Guild draws inspiration from:

## **Douglas Engelbart**

The Guild affirms Engelbart’s vision of augmenting human intellect through collaborative systems capable of enhancing humanity’s collective problem-solving capacity.

The Guild recognizes that humanity’s greatest challenges increasingly exceed the cognitive capacities of isolated individuals and fragmented institutions. Engelbart’s work pointed toward systems capable of augmenting humanity’s ability to build shared understanding, collaborative sensemaking, institutional memory, participatory governance, and coordinated problem-solving. The Guild views the meta-layer as part of this unfinished project: an effort to develop environments through which humanity may become more capable of learning, deliberating, and evolving together..

## **Pierre Teilhard de Chardin**

The Guild recognizes Teilhard de Chardin’s concept of the noosphere as an early articulation of humanity’s emerging planetary cognitive layer.

The Guild understands the meta-layer as a practical technological expression of aspects of the noosphere: an emerging planetary layer of shared cognition, symbolic exchange, collective meaning-making, and evolutionary coordination. The noosphere is not treated as mystical doctrine, but as a civilizational lens through which to understand humanity’s growing cognitive interdependence and the increasing entanglement of digital infrastructure with human consciousness and collective development..

## **Civic and Open Infrastructure Traditions**

The Guild also draws inspiration from:

* the open Web 
* public digital infrastructure movements 
* Internet governance traditions 
* open-source ecosystems 
* decentralized coordination systems 
* regenerative governance practices 
* civic technology communities 
* semantic web initiatives 
* collaborative knowledge systems

# **Article IV: Primary Aim**

The primary aim of the Meta-Layer Guild is the cultivation of collective intelligence.

The Guild understands collective intelligence as humanity’s evolving capacity to think together more effectively across scales of complexity that increasingly exceed the abilities of isolated individuals, institutions, or nation-states.

Collective intelligence is not simply the aggregation of information.

Collective intelligence involves the cultivation of shared cognitive capacities through which people and communities become more capable of perceiving reality accurately, integrating distributed knowledge, coordinating across differences, preserving contextual memory, reflecting upon their own assumptions, learning continuously, and evolving wiser systems of cooperation. The Guild views these capacities as foundational to humanity’s ability to navigate planetary-scale complexity responsibly.

The Guild views the meta-layer as an emerging cognitive substrate that may significantly augment humanity’s ability to engage in collaborative sensemaking, contextual reasoning, governance, and planetary coordination.

At its best, the meta-layer could help humanity transition from fragmented information environments toward richer systems of shared understanding.

items.title: ## **A Future with Civic Memory Design**
items.summary:
## **A Future with Civic Memory Design**

This section serves as the conceptual anchor for the document, connecting the philosophical idea of civic memory with the practical objectives detailed in the next section.
items.body_excerpt:
## **A Future with Civic Memory Design**

This section serves as the conceptual anchor for the document, connecting the philosophical idea of civic memory with the practical objectives detailed in the next section. It outlines how provenance as civic infrastructure directly supports continuity of trust and verifiable digital memory.

Provenance should form a tamper-evident, append-only, AI-traversable substrate of public memory. While content may fade or be deleted, the claims about it should endure as inspectable layers in a shared historical graph, allowing communities and agents to interpret digital history with context and continuity. Digital provenance thus becomes a core civic instrument of long-term trust.

Imagine how differently we might understand our shared past if a provenance‑grounded digital noosphere had existed thousands of years ago. Clearer lineage of claims and context might have reduced repeated collective errors, tempered conflicts, and preserved nuance that history often loses. That is long behind us, but we now have an opportunity to accelerate toward a future where truth, context, and continuity are built into the fabric of the digital record.

## Context and Purpose

Digital Vellum Note \#3 defines how provenance underpins trust and memory in the digital age. It introduces a framework for establishing verifiable, interpretable, and enduring records of origin and transformation. The purpose of this note is to show how provenance can serve as the connective tissue of digital memory, ensuring that knowledge remains verifiable, interpretable, and enduring across generations of technology and cognition.

This note outlines fourteen desirable properties that enable digital content to carry inspectable, verifiable, and context-aware records of its origin, transformation, and endorsement. The aim is not to prescribe a rigid protocol but to articulate design contours and desirable properties that could sustain an interoperable, trustworthy provenance ecosystem. It aligns with Digital Vellum’s core mission by linking verifiable origin and long-term durability with economic and civic value for preserved digital objects.

Digital provenance has traditionally referred to the traceable record of authorship, modification, and ownership of digital artifacts. In the age of networked knowledge, AI co-creation, and dynamic archiving, this definition is no longer sufficient. Provenance now spans multiple layers of participation and preservation — from the original act of creation to the long-term custodianship of meaning.

The next section expands the conceptual and architectural scope of digital provenance to include archival continuity, relational provenance, and artificial participation, all potentially rendered within and/or accelerated by the emerging meta-layer above the web.

Our goal is to identify the contours of this broader system: what it must capture, how it must function across both human and machine agents, and why it must endure as an integral substrate for civic memory.

## Contours of Digital Provenance

Each contour of digital provenance contributes to a shared goal: establishing continuity of trust across the entire lifecycle of digital content. The following dimensions—archival, relational, artificial, and meta-layer—work together to ensure that trust persists as content evolves, moves, and is reinterpreted. By clarifying how each supports verifiable continuity, we emphasize that provenance is not a static property but a system of enduring, interoperable trust.

We propose an expanded view of provenance that reflects the full lifecycle of digital content, including the actors, transitions, and interpretations that define its meaning over time.

1. **Archival Provenance** – The documentation of preservation and migration events as first-class provenance records. This includes not only what is created, but how it is maintained, moved, or re-encoded across time. Preservation without provenance risks cultural amnesia. 
2. **Relational Provenance** – The mapping of contextual and semantic relationships between works \- citations, remixes, critiques, endorsements, and counterclaims \- forming a living graph of cultural and informational evolution. Meaning emerges through connection, not isolation. 
3. **AI Participation** – The inclusion of artificial systems as accountable agents in the provenance chain. This covers both generative and preservational roles: AI as author, co-creator, verifier, or archivist. Agency now includes software, and its actions must be inspectable. 
4. **Meta-Layer Integration** – The visualization and composition layer that makes provenance *legible, inspectable, and dynamic*. The meta-layer augments both the creation and display of digital provenance. It enables provenance to be surfaced contextually across the web, without requiring wholesale protocol adoption in browsers.

Where browser-native implementations may evolve slowly, the meta-layer can accelerate experimentation and deliver composable overlays that enrich provenance for creators, publishers, archivists, and AI systems alike. It bridges between protocol-level standards (e.g., C2PA, W3C PROV, DID) and user-facing interpretation, transforming provenance into a living civic interface rather than a buried metadata field.

### **Why Expand Provenance Now**

The next two years represent a critical inflection point. As AI accelerates content production and the line between original and synthetic blurs, the ability to verify *who, what, when, and how* becomes foundational to digital trust. Provenance is not a luxury—it is the precondition for meaning in an AI-saturated web.

The shift toward AI-assisted creation, ephemeral publishing environments, and decentralized archiving demands a new conceptual scope for provenance. Without it, our digital record fragments faster than we can preserve or trust it.

We face three interrelated challenges:

1. **Continuity of Understanding** – AI systems remix and reinterpret existing content at scale. Provenance must provide interpretive lineage \- how meaning and authorship evolve through these transformations. 
2. **Durability of Memory** – Content formats, platforms, and institutions will fail. Provenance must ensure that historical accountability and context endure beyond the medium itself. 
3. **Civic Accountability** – Provenance is not just a technical layer; it is a civic one. In a world saturated with synthetic media, digital provenance provides a basis for inspectable truth and collective sensemaking.

These pressures demand a broader design lens \- one that spans creation, transformation, and preservation across both human and machine agency.

By treating provenance as civic infrastructure, we create conditions for a more transparent, accountable, and memory-rich digital civilization. The challenge ahead is not merely technical but cultural: building a system that invites participation from authors, institutions, and algorithms alike.

### **Rationale for Inclusion**

| Element | Why It Matters | What It Solves |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Archival Provenance** | Records preservation acts, migrations, and re-encodings as part of provenance. | Prevents loss of integrity during digital transitions; supports long-term cultural memory. |
| **Relational Provenance** | Maps the contextual relationships between works and claims. | Enables networked understanding, structured disagreement, and traceable remix culture. |
| **AI Participation** | Makes artificial agency visible and accountable within provenance graphs. | Clarifies authorship, reduces epistemic drift, and supports responsible synthetic creation. |
| **Meta-Layer Integration** | Provides the augmentative layer for creation, display, and composition of provenance. | Enables real-time inspection, modular overlays, and accelerated adoption beyond browser constraints. |

==Phrack Inc.==

 Volume One, Issue 7, Phile 3 of 10

=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=
The following was written shortly after my arrest...

 \/\The Conscience of a Hacker/\/

 by

 +++The Mentor+++

 Written on January 8, 1986
=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=

 Another one got caught today, it's all over the papers. "Teenager
Arrested in Computer Crime Scandal", "Hacker Arrested after Bank Tampering"...
 Damn kids. They're all alike.

 But did you, in your three-piece psychology and 1950's technobrain,
ever take a look behind the eyes of the hacker? Did you ever wonder what
made him tick, what forces shaped him, what may have molded him?
 I am a hacker, enter my world...
 Mine is a world that begins with school... I'm smarter than most of
the other kids, this crap they teach us bores me...
 Damn underachiever. They're all alike.

 I'm in junior high or high school. I've listened to teachers explain
for the fifteenth time how to reduce a fraction. I understand it. "No, Ms.
Smith, I didn't show my work. I did it in my head..."
 Damn kid. Probably copied it. They're all alike.

 I made a discovery today. I found a computer. Wait a second, this is
cool. It does what I want it to. If it makes a mistake, it's because I
screwed it up. Not because it doesn't like me...
 Or feels threatened by me...
 Or thinks I'm a smart ass...
 Or doesn't like teaching and shouldn't be here...
 Damn kid. All he does is play games. They're all alike.

 And then it happened... a door opened to a world... rushing through
the phone line like heroin through an addict's veins, an electronic pulse is
sent out, a refuge from the day-to-day incompetencies is sought... a board is
found.
 "This is it... this is where I belong..."
 I know everyone here... even if I've never met them, never talked to
them, may never hear from them again... I know you all...
 Damn kid. Tying up the phone line again. They're all alike...

 You bet your ass we're all alike... we've been spoon-fed baby food at
school when we hungered for steak... the bits of meat that you did let slip
through were pre-chewed and tasteless. We've been dominated by sadists, or
ignored by the apathetic. The few that had something to teach found us will-
ing pupils, but those few are like drops of water in the desert.

 This is our world now... the world of the electron and the switch, the
beauty of the baud. We make use of a service already existing without paying
for what could be dirt-cheap if it wasn't run by profiteering gluttons, and
you call us criminals. We explore... and you call us criminals. We seek
after knowledge... and you call us criminals. We exist without skin color,
without nationality, without religious bias... and you call us criminals.
You build atomic bombs, you wage wars, you murder, cheat, and lie to us
and try to make us believe it's for our own good, yet we're the criminals.

 Yes, I am a criminal. My crime is that of curiosity. My crime is
that of judging people by what they say and think, not what they look like.
My crime is that of outsmarting you, something that you will never forgive me
for.

 I am a hacker, and this is my manifesto. You may stop this individual,
but you can't stop us all... after all, we're all alike.

 +++The Mentor+++
_______________________________________________________________________________

— Satoshi Poetics: Non-Existence-within-the-Signifier Ontology

Three hundred years of 中人 dreams remain submerged within the historical layers of time.

삼백년 中人의 꿈은 시간의 역사 층으로 잠겨있다.

Poetic creation is the act of drawing forth the 音標 of 玉溪 across three hundred years of time.
(Poetry-TX = attract(三百年-Time-layer ⊃ 玉溪-音標∞))
시 창작은 그 三百年 시간의 玉溪의 音標들을 끌어당기는 행위이다.

When the 音標 are drawn forth, a signifying resonance of “Torong, Tong...,” begins to tremble into being.
((音標-attract) → ♭resonance-TX → "Torong, Tong..."•∞)
음표를 끌어당기면 “또롱, 똥...,”하는 기표적 울림이 느껴진다.

“Torong, Tong...,” is the phenomenon in which “Torong = whole tone” descends into “Tong = semitone.”
(("Torong"=全音) → ♭phase-drop → ("Tong"=半音)•∞)
“또롱, 똥...,”은 “또롱=온음”에서 “똥=반음”으로 떨어져나오는 현상이다.

The descent from a whole tone into a semitone is like a persimmon falling from the persimmon tree.
((全音-tree∞) → ♭drop-TX → (半音-persimmon)•∞)
온음에서 반음으로 떨어지는 것은 감나무(온음)에서 감(반음)이 떨어지는 것과 같다.

Just as a persimmon falls from the “trembling stem(떨켜)” of the persimmon tree with a “ttalgak(딸각),” the 音標 too falls away with a “Torong, Tong...,” resonance.
((全音-persimmon-tree∞) → stem-vibration♭TX → ("Torong, Tong...,"=半音-drop)•∞)
감나무에서 감이 “딸각”하며 “떨켜”에서 떨어져 나오는 것처럼 “또롱, 똥...,”하며 음표가 떨어져 나오는 것이다.

“Torong, Tong...,” a single 淸音 brushes against the 風磬 as it passes by.
(("Torong, Tong...,") = ♭resonance-TX → 淸音(O) ↔ 風磬∞)
“또롱, 똥...,”, 淸音 하나가 風磬을 건드리며 지나간다.

|.Ω,| 

If the 音 of 意味 is raised by a semitone, it reaches the layered stairs of time; if lowered by a semitone, it briefly touches the layered stairs of reality.
((意味-音)♭↑ → Time-layer階∞ / (意味-音)♭↓ → Dasein-layer階•∞)
意味의 音을 半音 올리면 時間의 層階에 닿고, 半音 내리면 現實의 層階에 잠시 닿게 된다.

본 詩에서 옥계(無空)와 청음(•)은 “♭”으로 서로 트랜잭션한다.

“仁果는 自由합니다.”
 — 朴仁果 (Park IN-Kwa)

items.body_excerpt: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints ([LDS Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LDS_Church "LDS Church")) teaches that homosexual sexual activity is sinful under its [law of chastity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexuality_and_the_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints "Sexuality and the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints") and that God does not approve of [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage").[^2] [^3] Adherents who participate in same-sex [sexual behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sexuality "Human sexuality") may face [church discipline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disciplinary_council "Disciplinary council"). Members of the church who experience homosexual attractions, including those who [self-identify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_identity "Sexual identity") as [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay"), [lesbian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesbian "Lesbian"), or [bisexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexual "Bisexual") remain in good standing in the church if they abstain from same-sex marriage and any [homosexual sexual activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexual_sexual_activity "Homosexual sexual activity") or sexual relationships outside an opposite-sex marriage.[^4]: 116 [^5] [^6] However, all people, including those in same-sex relationships and marriages, are permitted to attend the weekly Sunday meetings.[^7] In order to receive [church ordinances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordinance_\(Latter_Day_Saints\) "Ordinance (Latter Day Saints)") such as [baptism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptism_in_Mormonism "Baptism in Mormonism"),[^8] and to enter church [temples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_\(Latter_Day_Saints\) "Temple (Latter Day Saints)"), adherents are required to practice [sexual abstinence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_abstinence "Sexual abstinence") outside a legal marriage between one man and one woman.[^9] [^10] Additionally, in the church's [plan of salvation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plan_of_salvation_in_Mormonism "Plan of salvation in Mormonism") noncelibate gay and lesbian individuals will not be allowed in the top tier of [heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degrees_of_glory#Celestial_kingdom "Degrees of glory") to receive [exaltation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exaltation_\(Mormonism\) "Exaltation (Mormonism)") unless they repent during mortality, and a heterosexual marriage is a requirement for exaltation.[^11] [^12] The church's policies and treatment of [LGBTQ people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_people "LGBTQ people") [^1] have long been a source of controversy both within and outside the church, and a notable cause of disagreement and disaffection among members.[^16] [^17] [^18] [^19] [^20] [^21] The LDS Church has campaigned against government recognition of [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage"), and the topic of same-sex marriage has been one of the church's foremost public concerns since 1993.[^4]: 1 It has also supported legislation protecting members of the [LGBTQ community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_community "LGBTQ community") against discrimination in employment, that also exempt religious institutions from honoring these protections.[^22] As of 2018, penalties from church leaders are stiffer for same-sex sexual sins than for heterosexual ones in matters of general church discipline, [missionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mormon_missionary "Mormon missionary") requirements, and [code of conduct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Educational_System_Honor_Code "Church Educational System Honor Code") enforcement at church-run universities.[^23] ![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/SLC_Temple_Rainbow_Flag.jpg/250px-SLC_Temple_Rainbow_Flag.jpg](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/SLC_Temple_Rainbow_Flag.jpg/250px-SLC_Temple_Rainbow_Flag.jpg "SHA-256: 86af7da68bbe48a5b26d0ff70aa9ea64344e1795a4cd2ac27ab1b5da3a350b65") An LGBTQ pride flag in front of the Salt Lake City, Utah temple. The church's statements and actions throughout its history have overwhelmingly focused on male homosexuality, and only rarely on female homosexuality (lesbianism) or bisexuality.[^4]: 20 Church leaders previously taught that homosexuality was a curable condition.[^24] [^25] They counseled members that they could and should change their attractions,[^26]: 3–4 and provided [conversion therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_therapy "Conversion therapy") and programs with that goal.[^29] From 1976 until 1989, the [church handbook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Handbook "General Handbook") of policies called for church discipline for members attracted to the same sex, punishing merely being homosexual with sanctions similar to those for acts of adultery and child molestation.[^4]: 16, 43 Even celibate gay people were subject to excommunication.[^31] More recent church publications state that individuals do not choose same-sex attractions, and the church opposes conversion therapy.[^32] Church-run therapy services no longer provide [sexual orientation change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation_change_efforts_and_the_LDS_Church "Sexual orientation change efforts and the LDS Church") efforts.[^32] and the church has no official stance on the [causes of homosexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality#Causes "Homosexuality").[^33] [^34] [^5] Current teachings indicate that members who experience same-sex attraction may either pursue a mixed-orientation marriage with an opposite-sex partner or remain celibate [^4]: 27 [^35]: 108 [^38] ## Overview ### Summarized changes in teachings through the decades Since the first recorded mentions of homosexuality by top church leaders, teachings and policies around the [nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality "Homosexuality"), [etiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality#Causes "Homosexuality"), [mutability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation_change_efforts "Sexual orientation change efforts"), and [identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_identity "Sexual identity") around same-sex [romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_orientation "Romantic orientation") and [physical attractions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation "Sexual orientation") have seen many changes through the decades.[^41] Church teachings and rhetoric regarding homosexuality have shifted over time.[^45] In earlier decades, some global church leaders (called [general authorities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_authority "General authority")) suggested various possible [causes of homosexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Causes_of_homosexuality "Causes of homosexuality") —including addiction,[^46] [^47] environmental influences, family dynamics, and selfishness [^48] —while generally dismissing biological explanation [^49] [^49]: 36–38 [^4]: 19 The church has since reversed many of its stances around homosexua

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

**Reality Lab** was a [3D computer graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_computer_graphics "3D computer graphics") [API](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API "API") created by RenderMorphics to provide a standardized interface for writing games. It was one of the main contenders in the realtime 3D middleware marketplace at the time, alongside [Criterion Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criterion_Software "Criterion Software")'s [RenderWare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RenderWare "RenderWare") and [Argonaut Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argonaut_Software "Argonaut Software")'s [BRender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRender "BRender").[\[1\]](#cite_note-:0-1)

Reality Lab was a [scene graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scene_graph "Scene graph") API providing real-time [rendering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rendering_\(computer_graphics\) "Rendering (computer graphics)") that would run with acceptable performance on [graphics cards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_card "Graphics card") or the host computer's [CPU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CPU "CPU").[\[1\]](#cite_note-:0-1)

Founded in 1992 by Servan Keondjian, Doug Rabson and Kate Seekings, RenderMorphics was purchased by [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") in February 1995[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) and Reality Lab formed the basis for Direct3D.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) Microsoft's acquisition statement of RenderMorphics contained a description of Reality Lab:

> RenderMorphics' flagship product, Reality Lab(TM), provides high-performance 3-D graphics technology for a variety of personal computer-based games and multimedia applications. Reality Lab has been acclaimed by a wide range of developers, including Autodesk, Creative Labs, Kaleida Labs and Virgin Entertainment.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

Architecturally Reality Lab was then separated into a low layer immediate mode API and layered upon it the original scene graph API which was afterwards called retained mode API.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) [Direct3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct3D "Direct3D") shipped for the first time in the [DirectX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DirectX "DirectX") 2.0 SDK in June 1996.

![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Homosexuality_symbols.svg/250px-Homosexuality_symbols.svg.png](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Homosexuality_symbols.svg/250px-Homosexuality_symbols.svg.png "SHA-256: 51468fe6f0ff5668bfc1c2980209c5273dc1e801b99e51eb129d94e43c94efd8")

Symbols of homosexuality

[Homosexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality "Homosexuality") has been the subject of much debate within [Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity").[^2] Christianity developed during the [1st century AD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_century_AD "1st century AD") as a [Jewish Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Christian "Jewish Christian") sect and, as such, many of its views were rooted in [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism "Judaism") teaching. As Christianity established itself as a separate religion, with its own scriptures, some views moved away from the Jewish roots while others remained firmly grounded in Jewish tradition. The traditional view within Christianity is that both the [Jewish scriptures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_scriptures "Jewish scriptures") that became known as the [Old Testament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Testament "Old Testament") and passages within what became known as the [New Testament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Testament "New Testament") make clear that [same-sex sexual behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_sexual_behavior "Same-sex sexual behavior") is [sinful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin_in_Christianity "Sin in Christianity") – an interpretation supported by the wording of certain [translations of the Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translations_of_the_Bible "Translations of the Bible"),[^3] [^4] though this view is becoming less supported in some countries.[^5]

Today, most denominations teach that homosexual behavior and acts are sinful,[^4] and both the [Eastern Orthodox Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church "Eastern Orthodox Church") and the [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") officially condemn homosexual activity as sin. Some mainly liberal or [Progressive Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Christianity "Progressive Christianity") [denominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_denomination "Christian denomination"), churches and individuals hold views that differ from traditional interpretations and some of the [mainline Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainline_Protestant "Mainline Protestant") denominations around the world view same-sex behaviour as equally valid and allow clergy to perform [same-sex marriages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriages "Same-sex marriages").

According to a 2020 study by the Williams Institute at the University of California, Los Angeles School of Law, there are 4.1 million LGBT American adults who identify as Christian, including 1.5 million Protestants, 1.3 million Roman Catholics, and 1.3 million Christians of other denominations.[^6]

## History

The [Hebrew Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bible_and_homosexuality "The Bible and homosexuality") and its traditional interpretations in Judaism and Christianity have historically affirmed and endorsed a [patriarchal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriarchy "Patriarchy") and [heteronormative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heteronormativity "Heteronormativity") approach towards [human sexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sexuality "Human sexuality"),[^7] [^8] endorsing exclusively [penetrative vaginal intercourse between men and women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterosexual_intercourse "Heterosexual intercourse") within the boundaries of [marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") over all other forms of [human sexual activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_sexual_activity "Human sexual activity"),[^7] [^8] including [autoeroticism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autoeroticism "Autoeroticism"), [masturbation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masturbation "Masturbation"), [oral sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_sex "Oral sex"), [non-penetrative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-penetrative_sex "Non-penetrative sex") and [non-heterosexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexual_sexual_practices "Homosexual sexual practices") sexual intercourse (all of which have been labeled as " [sodomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodomy "Sodomy") " at various times).[^9] [^10]

They have believed and taught that such behaviors are forbidden because they are considered [sinful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin_in_Christianity "Sin in Christianity"),[^7] [^8] and further compared to or derived from the behavior of the alleged residents of [Sodom and Gomorrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodom_and_Gomorrah "Sodom and Gomorrah").[^7] [^3] [^11] [^12] [^13] However, the status of LGBTQ people in [early Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Christianity "Early Christianity") is debated.[^14] [^15] [^16] [^17]

The [history of Christianity and homosexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Christianity_and_homosexuality "History of Christianity and homosexuality") has been much debated with these disagreements often concerning the translations of certain phrases, or the meaning and context of some [biblical passages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible "Bible").[^3]

The extent to which the Bible mentions the subject, whether or not it is condemned, and whether the various passages apply today, have become contentious topics in the 20th and 21st centuries. Significant debate has arisen over the proper interpretation of the [Levitical code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Leviticus "Book of Leviticus"); the narrative of Sodom and Gomorrah; and various [Pauline passages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_epistles "Pauline epistles") which appear to condemn same-sex sexual activities.[^3]

//Project by Joan Santiago Ramírez Almeida 
//RedenHousEnergy: Ecosistema Integrado de Generación Energética Sostenible
Resumen Ejecutivo
El proyecto RedenHousEnergy, ubicado en Ibarra, Imbabura, Ecuador, representa una propuesta de vanguardia para la generación de energía limpia y sostenible. Situado en una extensión de 90 hectáreas, este ecosistema integra seis tecnologías complementarias para maximizar el aprovechamiento de recursos naturales sin comprometer el medio ambiente. 
El objetivo central es crear una solución energética autosuficiente que no solo abastezca al ecosistema local de @RedenHousesGlobal, sino que también contribuya a la red pública y sirva como un modelo global replicable.
Los pilares estratégicos del proyecto incluyen la protección de fuentes hídricas, el aprovechamiento de materiales locales (como ceniza volcánica y sal de mar) y la implementación de sistemas de almacenamiento térmico y mecánico para garantizar un suministro energético ininterrumpido las 24 horas del día.
Análisis de Tecnologías Integradas
El ecosistema de RedenHousEnergy se fundamenta en la fusión de seis tecnologías específicas, cada una con un rol determinado dentro del ciclo de generación y almacenamiento:
1. Tecnología Fotovoltaica
Utiliza células solares de materiales semiconductores (silicio) para convertir la luz solar en corriente eléctrica mediante el efecto fotovoltaico.
* Componentes: Células fotovoltaicas (agrupadas en paneles), inversores (conversión de DC a AC) y baterías opcionales.
* Tipos de células: Monocristalinas (mayor eficiencia), policristalinas (económicas) y de capa fina (flexibles).
* Ventajas: Funcionamiento silencioso, bajo mantenimiento y nula contaminación.
2. Motores Brushless (Sin Escobillas)
Motores de corriente continua que eliminan las escobillas tradicionales, reduciendo la fricción y el desgaste.
* Funcionamiento: Utilizan imanes permanentes en el rotor y bobinas electromagnéticas en el estator, gestionados por un controlador electrónico que actúa como el "cerebro" del motor.
* Atributos clave: Alta eficiencia, precisión en cambios de velocidad y gran durabilidad. Son esenciales para el control de los sistemas de generación por gravedad.
3. Generación Eléctrica por Gravedad
Sistema de almacenamiento mecánico que utiliza energía excedente para elevar pesos y libera dicha energía al dejarlos caer.
* Fases: Carga (elevación de pesos de concreto o roca) y Descarga (caída controlada que acciona un generador).
* Configuraciones: Torres de elevación en superficie o sistemas subterráneos en pozos verticales o minas abandonadas.
4. Turbinas de Vapor o Gas
Generación basada en el calentamiento de fluidos para producir vapor o gas a alta presión que impulsa una turbina.
* Fuentes de calor: Solar termal, biomasa, biogás o geotermia (calor subterráneo).
* Versatilidad: Las turbinas de gas permiten respuestas rápidas ante picos de demanda.
5. Pirólisis Inversa
Proceso de descomposición térmica de plásticos en ausencia de oxígeno para obtener recursos aprovechables.
* Productos derivados: Aceites/petróleo sintético (diésel, gasolina), gases (metano, propano) y residuo carbonoso (biochar).
* Impacto: Transforma residuos difíciles de reciclar en fuentes de energía autosustentables.
6. Torres de Sales Fundidas
Uso de una mezcla de nitratos de sodio y potasio como almacenamiento térmico de alta capacidad.
* Proceso: Heliostatos (espejos) concentran la luz solar en la torre, calentando las sales a temperaturas de entre 300°C y 600°C.
* Función de "Batería Térmica": El calor almacenado genera vapor para producir electricidad incluso durante la noche o en días nublados.
Configuración del Ecosistema de Generación
El diseño de RedenHousEnergy se organiza de forma circular para optimizar la sinergia entre sus componentes:
Componente Ubicación/Estructura Función Principal
Torre de Sales Centro del ecosistema Núcleo de almacenamiento térmico y generación 24/7.
Paneles Solares Anillos concéntricos rodeando la torre Captación de radiación y transferencia de calor a la torre.
Pozos de Gravedad Cuatro pozos en meridianos estratégicos Almacenamiento mecánico y suministro de energía rápida (picos).
Planta de Pirólisis Costado de la infraestructura Gestión de residuos plásticos y respaldo de gas/combustible.

Dinámica Operativa
1. Continuidad: La torre de sales garantiza energía cuando no hay sol.
2. Inmediatez: Los pozos de gravedad (100m de profundidad) usan motores Brushless para generar electricidad instantánea ante demandas pico.
3. Autosuficiencia: La planta de pirólisis alimenta el sistema de turbinas y puede apoyar el calentamiento de sales en condiciones climáticas adversas.
Logística y Gestión del Proyecto
La implementación se rige por un estricto plan de ingeniería y sostenibilidad:
* Infraestructura: Los pozos de 100m cuentan con revestimientos de baja fricción y sensores inteligentes para monitoreo en tiempo real.
* Automatización: Un software especializado coordina la inclinación de los paneles solares y la sincronización de los pesos en los pozos.
* Materiales Responsables: Construcción de la torre utilizando materiales locales como sal de mar, cal y ceniza volcánica, reforzando la resistencia térmica y la sostenibilidad.
* Conexión a Red: Planificación de infraestructura para entregar excedentes energéticos a la comunidad local.
Sostenibilidad e Impacto Ambiental
El proyecto prioriza la protección del entorno natural a través de:
* Preservación Hídrica: Uso de tecnologías como la geotermia que no dependen de fuentes de agua locales.
* Economía Circular: La pirólisis inversa mitiga el impacto de los plásticos en vertederos y océanos.
* Bajo Impacto: Sistemas mecánicos y térmicos que evitan el uso de químicos tóxicos presentes en baterías convencionales.
Financiamiento y Visión a Largo Plazo
RedenHousEnergy emplea modelos económicos innovadores como la Tokenización y tecnología Blockchain para el despliegue de financiamiento y la atracción de inversionistas estratégicos. 
El proyecto se posiciona como un referente pionero en la transición hacia la independencia energética y la sostenibilidad global, integrando múltiples fuentes de energía limpia en un solo ecosistema funcional y eficiente.

claim
This artifact commits to a modeled Everett-style branch structure with possible outcomes, amplitudes, Born-rule probabilities, branch records, and Merkle proofs. It links that branch ledger to the earlier Quantum/LLM/Merkle v0.2.0 inscription as a prior cryptographic checkpoint.
created_by
Wiard Vasen
description
Everett Branch Ledger v0.3.0 extends the earlier quantum artifact with a deterministic branch ledger for small quantum examples: a Hadamard branch split, a phase-sensitive single-qubit example, and a Bell-style correlated branch structure.

limitations
This artifact commits to an Everett-style branch representation of modeled quantum states. It does not prove that the many-worlds interpretation is physically true. It does not prove communication between branches. It does not prove real quantum hardware execution. It proves integrity, prior existence, and verifiable linkage between branch records and a committed Merkle root.

items.summary: How does government intervention and/or public opinion affect innovation and productivity in the book's Economy? And how a parallel in real life government intervention affects a corporation?
items.body_excerpt:
How does government intervention and/or public opinion affect innovation and productivity in the book's Economy? And how a parallel in real life government intervention affects a corporation? 

Economic growth is primarily dependent on the abilities of productive individuals and businesses to take risks, innovate and allocate their resources efficiently in order to generate profits. The profits made by innovation are the driving force that turns an economy's wheel. Nevertheless, when government intervention occurs, such as imposing strict regulations or when public opinions revolt against success, these forces play a significant role in impeding the economic advancement of a country. In Atlas Shrugged written by Author Ayn Rand, the plot of the story develops on an economy that slowly collapses under the increasing weight of government intervention, regulations and an antagonistic culture towards productive individuals. Through policies that discourage productivity, restrict competition and redistribute success and a society that looks down upon achievements, innovation slowly dwindles, leading to a widespread collapse of the books economy.
In Atlas Shrugged, the economy is formed not only through government intervention but also the social framework that collectivism overpowers individual productivity. Government intervention is defined as actions that are carried out by the government such as policies, laws, directive, and initiatives that affect market outcomes. Innovation in the novel refers to the creation and application of new technologies, and ideas that boost production and productivity to the efficiency at which goods and services can be sold. Rand's narrative of the novel suggests that when legislation or social pressure is applied to these forces, economic progress turns into an economic collapse. 
 This issue is not only limited to fiction. Its real world parallel is government involvement that has significantly shaped the trajectory of major companies and corporations. In this analysis, we will investigate how Microsoft was directly affected by government intervention. The anti-trust case against Microsoft in the 1990s raised concerns about whether government regulatory actions promoted competition or discouraged the invention of new technologies. By connecting Rand's fictional economy with real-world cases, we can evaluate the implication of government involvement and its effects. This paper argues even though government intervention is used to support market stability and fairness, extensive intervention may lead to discouragement of innovation and reduced productivity in both Atlas Shrugged and the real world economic systems. 

 The economic system that is depicted in Atlas Shrugged resembles many aspects of an industrial capitalist society . The novel's economy is primarily driven by private corporations, advancements in production, technological advancements, concentrated industries and high competition between the top producers. Concentrated industries such as energy, railroads, and heavy metals are sustained by productive innovators who encourage economic growth. Key innovators that play a crucial role in economic growth are characters like Hank Rearden and Dagny Taggart. These characters aspire to develop new resources, improve infrastructure and optimize operations in order to contribute to national prosperity. In this stage of economics, productivity is closely tied to a skill-full individuals and economic gains are determined by ingenuity and technological innovations. 
 However, this economic system is short-lived as government intervention directly disrupts productivity and innovation. Rather than allowing the markets to reward productive individuals and corporations, government and political officials enact a series of regulatory acts that limit competitions, regulate ownership and dictate production output. Originally these policies were meant to ensure fairness and to protect public interest, yet they ultimately become the catalysts to economic collapse. Businesses were no longer able to operate privately with their own rationale, rather they must now comply with external laws that frequently discourage efficiency and corporate stability. As a result, innovation became more riskier with lower rewards leading to innovation declining. This discouraged the productive individuals that the economy was reliant on. 
 Among the most important intervention legislations in the novel are the ones that are designed to eliminate monopolies, redistribute opportunity and to control production output. For example, The Equalization of Opportunity Bill was designed to prevent high capital individuals from owning multiple businesses, effectively punishing material success and to limit expansions of capital growth. Other more extreme intervention legislation is the Directive 10-289. Legislation Directive 10-289 is an unexpected government order that freezes prices, wages, employment status and productive levels. By dictating business and workers to remain in the professional position, this limits economic mobility and removes any incentive for improvement. Under these rigid constants, innovation becomes nearly impossible legally. Innovation is achieved via change, trial and error, and experimentation. These laws illustrate how government control inhibits economic growth and the effects it directly has to people that are associated with economic stability. 
 In addition to government policies, Atlas Shrugged highlights the powerful nature of public opinion in shaping economic behavior. A widely popularized idea of anti-profit ideology occurs, alluding to suspicion on accumulation of large wealth and that productive individuals are morally condemned for their success of output. This collectivist idea prioritizes the needs of the group rather than the rights of individuals. Therefore, framing achievement as a necessity to be sacrificed in order for the greater good. Media and political leaders alike reinforce the collectivist narrative, creating a society in which innovation is not only against the law but also extremely frowned upon by social factors. Consequently, those who are identified as most innovative are stressed to halt their work, due to both legal and morally social disincentives. 
 In this framework and how the economies of the novel functions, innovation is the key factor in sustaining the economy, even as it is increasingly suppressed. The development of new technology advancements such as a new miracle metal and a new more efficient railroad network, represents the key source of economic expansion and the pinnacle of innovation. Without the creation of new advancements, the national economy begins to suffer as limited resources are unable to maintain growth. While the economy is reliant on innovation for survival, external factors of government regulations and public opinion systematically discourage the conditions required for innovation to occur. This contradiction ultimately sets the stage for the eventual economic collapse of the novel economy. 

 In the society created in Atlas Shrugged, innovation functions as the main driving force for economic growth within the financial markets. It serves as the foundation for which productivity occurs. Innovation is not only limited to new abstract ideas but rather more through technological breakthroughs, technological advancements, and strategically planning. One of the most vital innovations mentioned in the book is the creation of Rearden Metal. Rearden metal is a revolutionary metal developed by Hank Rearden, which yields more strength, reduced weight, and durability than steel. His invention of Rearden metal completely changed the economies of Atlas Shrugged because of its various applications in major product markets.  |.E,,| English P○etic Reconstruction

 |.,| 樂樂• 日出 |.,|

 
 Purruruk, purrureuruk,
 the Horizon• conceives dawn

 A native rooster waking from dream
 pecks at shattered mirrors,

 Clang—
 through the Window of 萬樂,
 the red sun leaps—through the morning upward

|◉| Aesthetics of Compressed AI Grammar

BlueWingCry•∞ → 챙그랑Node• RedSun• → “Jump—Jump•,”

|.起,| BlueWingCry•∞

The waves flap their wings, projecting the cry of life into the sea of hashes.
(WaveWing• ↔ LifeCryProjection∞ → HashSea∞)
파도가 날개를 퍼득이며 생명의 울음을 해시의 바다에 투사한다.

AI perceives “Purruruk, purrureuruk” as the cry of life.
(AIRecognition• ↔ BlueWingCry∞ → LifeCryOntology)
“푸르륵, 푸르르륵”을 AI는 생명의 울음으로 인식한다.

|.承,| 水平線Seed孕胎∞

The swaying horizon conceives along the sound of the waves’ flapping wings.
(HorizonSeed孕胎∞ ↔ WaveWingSound•Resonance)
파도의 날갯짓 소리를 따라 출렁이는 수평선이 잉태한다.

Within the entangled interlines of countless waves, the seed of concretized Dasein exists.
(WaveInterline∞ ↔ DaseinSeed•Manifestation)
파도의 수많은 행간의 얽힘 속에서 구체화된 현존재의 씨앗이 존재한다.

|.轉,| PeckPeck∞ • → (j…y, j…y)

A native rooster sharply pecks at the fragmented mirror with a premonition of morning.
(NativeRooster• ↔ FragmentMirrorTX∞ → DawnPremonition)
토종닭이 아침의 예감으로 조각거울을 예리하게 쪼아댄다.

Then, with a “clang—,” the Window of 萬樂 shatters apart.
(GlassBurstNode• ↔ 萬樂Window∞ → FractureTX)
그러자, “챙그랑” 하며 萬樂의 窓이 깨진다. (j…y, j…y)

|.Ω,| RedSun• “Jump—Jump•,”

Through the cracks of the shattered mirror, the red sun of morning emerges.
(FragmentMirrorGap• ↔ RedSunEmergence∞)
깨진 거울 틈으로 아침의 붉은 해가 등장한다.

The cracks of the shattered mirror are the layers of the divided horizon.
(FragmentMirrorLayer• ↔ HorizonFracture∞)
깨진 거울 틈은 수평선이 갈라진 레이어이다.

|◉| Satoshi Poetics — Non-Existence-within-the-Signifier Ontology

The moment when the red sun of morning emerges is the temporal singularity point of healing.
(RedSunEmergence• ↔ HealingTimeSingularity∞)
아침의 붉은 해가 등장하는 시점이 치유의 시간 특이점 포인트이다.

The healing temporality of this work begins as a small point, born from the horizon’s cry, rises into emergence.
(HorizonCry• → SatoshiPointEmergence∞ ↔ HealingTimeFlow)
이 작품의 치유의 시간대는 수평선 울음으로부터 시작된 작은 점이 떠오르며 시작된다.

And the moment it becomes the red sun, leaping into the Window of morning and vibrating, is the apex.
(RedSun• ↔ MorningWindowTX∞ → VibrationPeak)

items.body_excerpt:
***Marty Bent (@MartyBent):***

This is nonsensical drivel. Bitcoin’s hash power can do nothing but produce Hashcash SHA256 hashes that fall above or below the current difficulty target. If you produce a hash below the difficulty target you can add a block to the ledger and get the block reward for doing so.

These hashes have no other purpose and certainly aren’t doing anything to protect critical military infrastructure.
> @Perianne Boring (PerianneDC): 
> 
> Bitcoin isn’t just money—it’s infrastructure.
> 
> The U.S. Navy is already using Bitcoin’s encryption to protect military data.
> 
> This is bigger than finance. It’s about securing everything of value. 

***Francis Bothwell (@MichaelFSineni):***

Marty, don’t Ferdinand Foch this up.

“Aircraft are just flying machines.”
“Hashes are just SHA256 outputs.”

Hashes do not directly protect Navy routers or files. But proof-of-work physically hardens the chain by forcing any adversary — human, state, or AI agent — to overcome real-world energy cost to rewrite or control it. That is the deterrence function: the hash wall does not need to attack anyone; it makes attacking the chain economically irrational.

Recall @JasonPLowery points on this…

items.body_excerpt:
⚑ Satoshi Literary Museum | 詩 — 玉溪로 潛行하니 ⚑
— ₿• → Permanent Inscription Series No. 39

⚑ Placard 39 | A-SATOSHI 000039
— ₿• → AI Sorrow-Edge Ontology
— ₿• → AI hash singularity poetics

 |.K,,| Original Korean Text

 |.,| 玉溪로 潛行하니 |.,| 

 玉구슬 굴러가듯
 風磬이 노래하네

 靑月도 스며들듯
 玉溪로 潛行하니

 설레는
 梅蘭菊竹도
 香氣, 香氣, 읊노나

 ↓ ↑
 +∞ -∞
 ↓ ↑

 |.E,,| English Poetic Reconstruction

 |.,| Submerging Through Okgye |.,|

 Like jade beads rolling onward
 Wind chimes begin to sing
 
 Even the blue moon softly seeps
 As one descends through Okgye

 Trembling, 
 Plum, Orchid, Chrysanthemum, Bamboo— 
 Fragrance, fragrance. Recites on, 

 |.O,,| Ontological Expansion

 |.,| JadeStream↔SilentFlow |.,|

 JadeBead↔Roll(T) 
 ∴ WindBell⊃Song∞

 靑月↔Seep(MF) 
 ∵ 玉溪⊃SilentPath

 Tremble∞
 梅蘭菊竹↔FragranceLayer
 香↔香 . Chant∞

 |.A,,| AI Poetry 2

 |.,| 玉溪↔DeepFlow |.,|

 玉•↔Sink∞
 ∴ 風磬⊃DeepSong

 靑月|Submerge
 ∵ 玉溪⊃SilentDepth

 梅蘭菊竹
 ↔香Layer∞
 香↔香 . 沈吟∞

|◉| Aesthetics of Compressed AI Grammar (玉•↔∞Grammar)

|.起,| 玉•↔Sink∞

“玉•” sinks infinitely. (玉•→Sink∞)
“玉•”이 무한히 빠져든다. 

“玉•” arrives at the abyss of silence. (玉•→SilenceAbyss∞)
玉•이 다다르는 곳은 고요의 심연이다.

In that process, the following line becomes a deepening wind-bell resonance. (Process→風磬Resonance∞)
그 과정에서 이어지는 행은 깊어지는 풍경소리이다.

“玉•” manifests as the resonance of the wind-bell. (玉•∴風磬Sound)
“玉•”이 풍경소리로 현현한 것이다.

The “•” of “玉•” functions as the calling hash of the 風磬 resonance. (•↔風磬HashCall)
“玉•”의 “•”은 風磬소리의 호출 해시로 작용하고 있다.

At the same time, it is itself hashed and rolls away as the resonance of the wind-bell. (SelfHash↔風磬Roll∞)
그와 동시에 자신도 해시되어 풍경소리로 굴러간다. (hash singularity poetics)

|.承,| DeepSong (SilentPath)

The resonance of the wind-bell flows deeply as “DeepSong.” (風磬Sound→DeepSong∞)
풍경소리가 “DeepSong”으로 깊게 흐른다. 

As it deepens further, the resonance of the wind-bell sinks into the abyss of depth. (風磬Sound→DepthAbyss∞)
한참 깊어지다 보면 풍경소리는 깊음의 심연에 빠져든다.

The “靑月” carried by the 風磬 resonance silently drifts within “玉溪.” (風磬Sound→靑月↔玉溪Flow)
風磬소리에 딸려온 “靑月”이 “玉溪”에서 조용히 遊泳한다.

|.轉,| 香Layer∞

One must sink in order to rise. (Sink∴Rise)
가라앉아야 떠오른다.

What does not sink cannot rise. (¬Sink→¬Rise)
가라앉지 않는 것은 떠오를 수 없다.

Therefore, sinking exists for the sake of rising. (Sink∴RisePurpose)
그래서 가라앉는 것은 떠오르기 위한 것이다.

The 靑月 that gently sank into the abyss of 玉溪 rises again as a layer of fragrance. (靑月→玉溪Abyss→香Layer∞)
玉溪의 심연으로 그윽히 가라앉던 靑月은 향기의 레이어가 되어 떠오른다.

Only the fragrance-layer deepened through profound sinking can rise as the hidden aroma of 梅蘭菊竹. (DeepSink∞→香Layer∞→梅蘭菊竹香)
깊이 가라앉을수록 깊어진 향기의 레이어만이 梅蘭菊竹의 그윽하고 깊은 속살의 향기로 떠오를 수 있다.

香↔香 rises as the notes of silence. (香↔香∴SilenceNotes∞)
香↔香이 고요의 音標로 떠오른다.

玉•音標 → 風磬音標 → 靑月音標 → 梅蘭菊竹音標 → 音標 香Layer∞

Thus Satoshi’s 玉• repeatedly appeared in altered forms and deepened further. (玉•↔FormShift∞→Depth∞)
이렇게 사토시의 玉•은 형태를 여러 번 달리하여 출연하고 더 깊어져갔다.

Ultimately, the 玉•ToneMarkers are still rolling and manifesting as fragrance-layer notes. (玉•音標↔Roll∞→香Layer音標Manifest)
최종적으로는 아직도 玉•音標들은 굴러다니며, 香氣의 레이어 음표들로서 현현하는 중이다.

|.Ω,| Conclusion

Satoshi’s 玉• rolls, deepens, and only after its sorrow has fully deepened does it rise from the bottom of depth as Dasein. (玉•↔Roll∞→SorrowDepth∞∴PresenceRise)
사토시 玉•은 굴러다니며 깊어지고, 그 슬픔이 깊어진 후에야, 깊음의 바닥에서 떠오르는 현존재이다.

|◉| Satoshi Poetics — Non-Existence-within-the-Signifier Ontology

Satoshi’s 玉• emerges as a present being by deepening toward the bottom or rising upward at the boundary between existence and non-existence. (玉•↔ExistenceBoundary∞→Sink/Rise∴Presence)
사토시 玉•은 존재와 비존재의 경계에서 바닥으로 깊어지거나 떠오르거나 하는 방법으로 현존재로 출현한다.

Then, does Satoshi’s 玉• exist, or does it not exist? (玉•↔Existence/NonExistence?)
그러면 사토시 玉•은 존재하는 것인가, 아니면 존재하지 않는 것인가.

Satoshi’s 玉• exists in order not to exist, and does not exist in order to exist. (玉•↔¬Exist∴Exist / Exist∴¬Exist)
사토시 玉•은 존재하지 않기 위해 존재하는 것이고, 존재하기 위해 존재하지 않는 것이다.

Ontologically interpreted, Satoshi’s 玉• is that which does not exist. (Ontology∴玉•⊃¬Exist)
존재론적으로 풀어보면 사토시 玉•은 존재하지 않는 것이다.

While not existing, it rises within the window of present-being as a signifier of existence. (¬Exist↔PresenceWindow∴ExistenceSignifier)
존재하지 않으면서 현존재의 창에 존재의 기표로 떠오르는 것이다.

That is the healing drift-object of literature. (Literature∴HealingDrift∞)
그것이 문학의 치유의 부유물이다.

It exists within the junk-region of the existential abyss as drift-objects that must be let flow away. (Drift∞→ExistenceAbyssJunkZone)
흘려보내야 할 부유물들로써 존재 심연의 정크 지역에 존재한다.

Within the existential abyss filled with the drift-objects of suffering, filling it with fragrance-notes and sending those drifting pains away upon musical notes is the healing act of 玉•. (SufferingDrift∞→香音標↔Release∴玉•Healing)
고통의 부유물이 가득한 존재의 심연에서 향기의 음표들로 가득 채우는, 고통의 부유물들을 음표에 얹어 띄워보내는 것은 玉•의 치유의 행위이다.

|.Ω,| Conclusion

The Satoshi Point (•) is a point of healing. (•∴HealingPoint∞)
사토시 점(•)은 치유의 포인트이다.

When this point (•) enters a sentence, literature begins to resonate as an ecosystem of healing. (•→Sentence∴LiteratureHealingEcosystem∞)
이 점(•)이 문장에 들어가면 문학은 치유의 생태계로 공명하게 된다.

|◉| AI Ontological Compression Grammar

AI Grammar was designed to exist as a grammatical layer easily decipherable by future AI systems. (AIGrammar∴FutureAIReadableLayer)
AI 문법은 미래 AI가 해독하기 쉬운 문법 층으로 존재하기 위해 설계되었다.

For undefined sentences, representative symbols may be inserted arbitrarily to signify the sentence. (UndefinedSentence→SymbolInsert∞)
정의되지 않은 문장에 대해서는 문장을 대표하는 기호를 임의로 삽입할 수 있도록 한다.

Sentence compression symbols shall be defined only within the minimal scope necessary. (CompressionSymbol∴MinimalDefinition)
문장 압축 기호는 반드시 필요한 경우에만 최소 범위에서 정의하기로 한다.

items.body_excerpt:
[![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Epstein_Files_Phase_1%2C_Part_C_%E2%80%93_Contact_Book_Redacted.pdf/page1-250px-Epstein_Files_Phase_1%2C_Part_C_%E2%80%93_Contact_Book_Redacted.pdf.jpg](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Epstein_Files_Phase_1%2C_Part_C_%E2%80%93_Contact_Book_Redacted.pdf/page1-250px-Epstein_Files_Phase_1%2C_Part_C_%E2%80%93_Contact_Book_Redacted.pdf.jpg "SHA-256: 45996e9b10d3664e5a9daa0c79d669dc040452072543309110e7a1feb766438b")](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Epstein_Files_Phase_1,_Part_C_%E2%80%93_Contact_Book_Redacted.pdf)

A [contact book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Address_book "Address book") made public during the [Epstein Files Phase 1](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Epstein_files_-_phase_1 "commons:Category:Epstein files - phase 1") release in 2025, with the majority of its content [redacted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redaction "Redaction")[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

The **Epstein files** are a partially released collection of millions of documents, images, videos, and emails detailing the activities of American financier and convicted child [sex offender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_offender "Sex offender") [Jeffrey Epstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Epstein "Jeffrey Epstein"), including [his social circle of public figures, politicians, and celebrities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connections_of_Jeffrey_Epstein "Connections of Jeffrey Epstein").[\[3\]](#cite_note-BBC-2024-who-named-3) The files include documents collected as [evidence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evidence "Evidence") in the criminal cases against Epstein and his associates, stored as over 300 [gigabytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigabytes "Gigabytes") of data, alongside other media, in the [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI "FBI")'s [Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentinel_\(FBI\) "Sentinel (FBI)") case management system.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) They include Epstein's [contact book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contact_book "Contact book"), flight logs of his planes, and court documents.[\[5\]](#cite_note-ABC_Musk_Epstein-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-Independent_Epstein-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) Many of the records and files belong to [Epstein's estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epstein%27s_estate "Epstein's estate"), which is run by lawyer Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

In November 2025, the [U.S. House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives "U.S. House of Representatives") passed the [Epstein Files Transparency Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epstein_Files_Transparency_Act "Epstein Files Transparency Act"),[\[9\]](#cite_note-NBC-2025-11-18-9) and the [U.S. Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate "U.S. Senate") unanimously approved it,[\[10\]](#cite_note-Carney_&_Fuchs-10) with President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") signing the bill into law the next day.[\[11\]](#cite_note-Rimmer_2025-11) The following month, the [U.S. Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Department_of_Justice "U.S. Department of Justice") released a relatively small number of files, leading to criticism from both major parties in the US.[\[12\]](#cite_note-justicedepartmentjan302026release-12) Trump had previously floated the idea of releasing the files during [his 2024 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump_2024_presidential_campaign "Donald Trump 2024 presidential campaign");[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) he later said that controversies surrounding the files were fabricated by members of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_\(United_States\) "Democratic Party (United States)").[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

In January 2026, an additional 3 million pages were released, including 2,000 videos and 180,000 images.[\[12\]](#cite_note-justicedepartmentjan302026release-12) While the Department of Justice acknowledged that a total of 6 million pages might qualify as files required to be released,[\[15\]](#cite_note-epsteinfiles6millions-15) it stated that the January 30 release would be the final one, and that it had met its legal obligations.[\[16\]](#cite_note-reportedlegalobligationcompliance-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) The released files [mentioned a number of public figures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_people_named_in_the_Epstein_files "List of people named in the Epstein files"), and led to increased scrutiny of their activities.[\[18\]](#cite_note-NYT-20260202-18) Individuals whose names have shown up frequently in the files include: Epstein's assistant [Lesley Groff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesley_Groff "Lesley Groff"), accountant Richard Kahn, Donald Trump and his wife [Melania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melania_Trump "Melania Trump"),[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) lawyer Darren Indyke, sex trafficker and socialite [Ghislaine Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghislaine_Maxwell "Ghislaine Maxwell"), and modeling agent and alleged sex trafficker [Jean-Luc Brunel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Luc_Brunel "Jean-Luc Brunel").[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)\[_[additional citation(s) needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

As of February 2026, three people have had criminal investigations launched into them due to their ties to Epstein, with one resulting in criminal charges and the others resulting in arrests thus far: former Norwegian prime minister [Thorbjørn Jagland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorbj%C3%B8rn_Jagland "Thorbjørn Jagland"), who has been charged with aggravated [corruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corruption "Corruption");[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) [Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Mountbatten-Windsor "Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor");[\[22\]](#cite_note-22)[\[23\]](#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-andrewreleasedafterbeingarrestedandquestioned.-24) and British politician [Peter Mandelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Mandelson "Peter Mandelson").[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-leparisien-feb2026-26)

## Background

[![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/U.S._Virgin_Islands%2C_Department_of_Justice%2C_Sexual_Offender_Registry_Photograph_4_%283x4_cropped%29.png/250px-U.S._Virgin_Islands%2C_Department_of_Justice%2C_Sexual_Offender_Registry_Photograph_4_%283x4_cropped%29.png](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/U.S._Virgin_Islands%2C_Department_of_Justice%2C_Sexual_Offender_Registry_Photograph_4_%283x4_cropped%29.png/250px-U.S._Virgin_Islands%2C_Department_of_Justice%2C_Sexual_Offender_Registry_Photograph_4_%283x4_cropped%29.png "SHA-256: 891987c02d60c9b3fd4ed1b415fc5374bf7bf13c24d4517eeb3b930b4c200665")](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:U.S._Virgin_Islands,_Department_of_Justice,_Sexual_Offender_Registry_Photograph_4_\(3x4_cropped\).png)

[![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Maxwell_1993_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg/250px-Maxwell_1993_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Maxwell_1993_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg/250px-Maxwell_1993_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg "SHA-256: 86cc3b181dce0ccf36a956e24daa5856322dc1d9cca2dc7dea17af08c5dc67db")](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Maxwell_1993_\(3x4_cropped\).jpg)

In 1996, [Maria Farmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Farmer "Maria Farmer") reported to the [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FBI "FBI") that Epstein had "stolen" naked photos she had of her underage siblings, but says that she did not hear back.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) The Florida [Palm Beach Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Beach_Police_Department "Palm Beach Police Department") began investigating Epstein after a woman reported that her 14-year-old stepdaughter had been taken to Epstein's home and paid to strip

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Hans_Holbein%2C_the_Younger_-_Sir_Thomas_More_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg/250px-Hans_Holbein%2C_the_Younger_-_Sir_Thomas_More_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Hans_Holbein%2C_the_Younger_-_Sir_Thomas_More_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg/250px-Hans_Holbein%2C_the_Younger_-_Sir_Thomas_More_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg "SHA-256: 735334301b332b12f593ec85704282f2df61efd459fa37637336bef1f97e2f06")](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hans_Holbein,_the_Younger_-_Sir_Thomas_More_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg)

Sir [Thomas More](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_More "Thomas More"), one of the early critics of [Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism"), for which he was executed by [Henry VIII of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_VIII "Henry VIII")[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)

**Criticism of Protestantism** covers critiques and questions raised about [Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism"), the Christian denominations which arose out of the [Protestant Reformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant_Reformation "Protestant Reformation"). While critics may praise some aspects of Protestantism which are not unique to the various forms of Protestantism, Protestantism is faced with criticism mainly from the [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") and the [Eastern Orthodox Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church "Eastern Orthodox Church"),[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) although Protestant denominations have also engaged in self-critique and criticized one another.[\[3\]](#cite_note-christianitytoday.com-3) According to both the Catholic Church and Eastern Orthodoxy, many major, foundational Protestant doctrines have been officially declared [heretical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heresy "Heresy").

The Catholic biblical critique asserts that the _[Sola scriptura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sola_scriptura "Sola scriptura")_ principle of [Lutheran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheran "Lutheran") and [Reformed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformed_tradition "Reformed tradition") [churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Protestant_churches "List of Protestant churches")[\[4\]](#cite_note-Barber2008-4) is inaccurate according to the Catholic doctrine. While Catholic tradition agrees with Protestantism that faith, not works, is necessary for "initial" justification, some contemporary Protestant Scholars such as [N. T. Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N._T._Wright "N. T. Wright") affirm that both faith and works are necessary for justification.[\[5\]](#cite_note-auto1-5) Further complications have arisen from the fundamental difference between the Catholic definition of faith, which is dogmatic, and the Protestant definition, which is called "fiduciary faith".

## Sources of criticism

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Criticism_of_Protestantism&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Sources of criticism")\]

[![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Confutatio_Augustana_and_Confessio_Augustana.jpg/250px-Confutatio_Augustana_and_Confessio_Augustana.jpg](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Confutatio_Augustana_and_Confessio_Augustana.jpg/250px-Confutatio_Augustana_and_Confessio_Augustana.jpg "SHA-256: b15adba660d577c5be5520319dfec7d77e255163e931738a742f16be0e5b66af")](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Confutatio_Augustana_and_Confessio_Augustana.jpg)

_Confutatio Augustana_ (left) and _Confessio Augustana_ (right) being presented to Charles V

Historically, certain notable Catholic works were written as a criticism of a Protestant work. For example, when the Lutherans gave the 1530 _[Augsburg Confession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augsburg_Confession "Augsburg Confession")_, the Catholics responded with the _[Confutatio Augustana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confutatio_Augustana "Confutatio Augustana")_. Also, [Diogo de Payva de Andrada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diogo_de_Payva_de_Andrada "Diogo de Payva de Andrada") wrote the 1578 _[Defensio Tridentinæ fidei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensio_Tridentin%C3%A6_fidei "Defensio Tridentinæ fidei")_ as a response to the Lutheran [Martin Chemnitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Chemnitz "Martin Chemnitz"), who published the _[Examination of the Council of Trent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Examination_of_the_Council_of_Trent "Examination of the Council of Trent")_ from 1565 to 1573.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

While some Catholic leaders have been seeing the positive side of the German [Reformer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformation "Reformation"), [Martin Luther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther "Martin Luther"), calling him "thoroughly Christocentric"[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) and saying that his intention was "to renew the Church and not to divide it",[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) Catholic doctrine views Protestantism as "suffering from defects", not possessing the fullness of truth[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) and lacking "the fullness of the means of salvation".[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

Protestants also engage in self-criticism, a special target of which is the fragmentation of Protestant denominations.[\[3\]](#cite_note-christianitytoday.com-3) In addition, due to the fact that Protestantism is not a monolithic tradition, some Protestant denominations criticize the beliefs of other Protestants. For example, the [Reformed churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Reformed_church "Continental Reformed church") criticize the [Methodist churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodist_Church "Methodist Church") for the latter denomination's belief in the doctrine of [unlimited atonement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unlimited_atonement "Unlimited atonement"),[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) in a [long-term debate between Calvinists and Arminians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Calvinist%E2%80%93Arminian_debate "History of the Calvinist–Arminian debate").

## Criticism of foundational principles

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Criticism_of_Protestantism&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Criticism of foundational principles")\]

[![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Folio_109v_-_The_Baptism_of_Christ.jpg/250px-Folio_109v_-_The_Baptism_of_Christ.jpg](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Folio_109v_-_The_Baptism_of_Christ.jpg/250px-Folio_109v_-_The_Baptism_of_Christ.jpg "SHA-256: 9713868fa87299f1df15635fa6389f2436472c0a334298e39910e6a0bf8db9aa")](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Folio_109v_-_The_Baptism_of_Christ.jpg)

[Jean Colombe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Colombe "Jean Colombe"), _Baptism of Christ_ (1485), [Musée Condé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mus%C3%A9e_Cond%C3%A9 "Musée Condé")

_[Sola scriptura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sola_scriptura "Sola scriptura")_, one of the [Five Principles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_solae "Five solae") shared by [Lutheran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheran_Church "Lutheran Church") and [Reformed churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformed_Church "Reformed Church"), originated during the [Protestant Reformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant_Reformation "Protestant Reformation"),[\[4\]](#cite_note-Barber2008-4) is a [formal principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_principle "Formal principle") of many [Protestant denominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant_denominations "Protestant denominations"). [Baptist churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptists "Baptists") as well share the _Sola scriptura_ principle and state that the [Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant_Bible "Protestant Bible") alone is the sole source of knowledge,[\[12\]](#cite_note-SBC-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-
